features.description: A detailed technical plan in docs/plan/ covers the architecture, modules, data structures, public APIs and a task breakdown for all 15 milestones.
steps: Open docs/plan/ and its index file
Verify it describes every package listed in Architecture guidance with its responsibility and the dependency rules between packages
Verify it defines the key data structures and public API sketches: engine, camera, sources, layers, renderer interface, cache stores, network policies and framework adapters
Verify it contains a task breakdown for each of the 15 milestones, mapped to that milestone's acceptance criteria
Verify it defines the reference desktop and tablet devices and the per-frame CPU/GPU, memory and bundle-size budgets derived from Performance and quality targets

features.section: Working method for a multi-session build
features.description: All session state lives in files and git (feature_list.json, progress.md, init.sh, CLAUDE.md, an open-questions file and a follow-up list), so a fresh session resumes exactly where the last one stopped.
steps: From a fresh clone, run ./init.sh and confirm it installs dependencies, builds every package, starts the playground and runs the tests, exiting with code 0
Run npm run status and confirm it prints how many feature_list.json entries pass and how many fail
Open progress.md and confirm the latest session entry records what changed, which features changed status and the next step
Open the open-questions file and confirm each owner-only blocker names the stub or mock used meanwhile; open the follow-up list and confirm it collects ideas beyond the plan's scope
Run git status at the end of a session and confirm the working tree is clean and the build and tests pass

features.section: Working method for a multi-session build
features.description: An automated integrity check guarantees that feature_list.json entries are never deleted or reworded: only their status field may change.
steps: Run the feature-list integrity check (locally and in CI) and confirm it passes on the current file
In a scratch branch, reword one entry's description and confirm the check fails
In a scratch branch, delete one entry and confirm the check fails
In a scratch branch, change only one entry's status and confirm the check passes

features.description: Architecture decisions are recorded as ADRs in docs/adr/ from a template with context, options considered, decision and consequences, listed in an index.
steps: Open docs/adr/ and confirm an index lists every ADR with its number, title and status
Confirm the template has the sections Context, Options considered, Decision and Consequences, and that every existing ADR follows it
Confirm the ADR conventions require performance-related ADRs to record the profiling measurements taken before and after the change
Confirm CLAUDE.md points to the ADR conventions

features.description: Known bugs are tracked in one known-bugs list, and every bug fix starts with a failing regression test that reproduces it.
steps: Open the known-bugs list and confirm each entry has an id, symptom, reproduction, status and the name of its regression test
Confirm CLAUDE.md states the regression-first rule and the rule that no known bug may remain open at the end of a milestone

For a fixed bug in git history (or, if none exists yet, a bug planted in a scratch branch), run its regression test against the code before the fix and confirm it fails; with the fix confirm it passes

features.description: docs/research/ has an index of every problem area with its survey status and the study rules: open-source projects only, source-available projects with restrictive licenses excluded, study only and never copy code.
steps: Open the docs/research/ index and confirm it lists every problem area of the Research survey (precision, depth, terrain and imagery levels of detail, tile scheduling and caching, globe-to-flat transitions, camera control, picking, labels, atmosphere, GPU resource management, worker usage) plus sources, offline, vector tiles and 3D Tiles, and testing practices, each with a status
Confirm the rules state that only open-source projects are studied, that Mapbox GL JS from version 2 and Unreal Engine are excluded, and that no code is copied
Confirm the index lists, per area, the projects from the Research survey table to study

features.description: The research survey on floating-point precision (vertex jitter, relative-to-center, relative-to-eye, emulated double precision) is written in docs/research/ with the chosen approach justified.
steps: Open the precision survey in docs/research/
Verify it explains how CesiumJS, deck.gl, iTowns, OpenGlobus, 3DTilesRendererJS, MapLibre GL JS and osgEarth avoid vertex jitter, based on their code
Verify it lists jitter-related bugs and complaints from those projects' issue trackers, with links
Verify it summarizes how those projects test precision (unit tests, render tests, benchmarks)
Verify it compares the approaches with their trade-offs and known failure modes, and states the chosen approach and why, linking the ADR
Run a code-similarity scan of the repository against the studied projects' sources and confirm no copied code appears

features.description: The research survey on depth precision (z-fighting, logarithmic depth, reversed depth, multi-frustum rendering) is written in docs/research/ with the chosen approach justified.
steps: Open the depth survey in docs/research/
Verify it explains how CesiumJS, three.js, Babylon.js, Filament, Godot, osgEarth and iTowns handle near and far geometry in one view, based on their code
Verify it lists z-fighting, depth-precision and depth-related performance issues from their issue trackers, with links
Verify it summarizes how those projects test depth correctness
Verify it compares the approaches on both WebGPU and WebGL2, with trade-offs and known failure modes, and states the chosen approach and why, linking the ADR

features.description: The research survey on terrain and imagery levels of detail (quadtrees, screen-space error, chunked LOD, geometry clipmaps, geomorphing, skirts, RTIN meshes) is written in docs/research/ with the chosen approach justified.
steps: Open the levels-of-detail survey in docs/research/

Verify it explains how CesiumJS, osgEarth, iTowns, OpenGlobus, NASA WorldWind, 3DTilesRendererJS and MapLibre GL JS select and refine imagery and terrain tiles, and covers Ulrich's chunked LOD, Losasso and Hoppe's geometry clipmaps, Martini and Delatin
Verify it lists popping, crack, seam, hole and over-refinement issues from those projects' issue trackers, with links
Verify it summarizes how those projects test and benchmark tile selection
Verify it states the chosen selection, fallback and transition approach and why, linking the ADR

features.description: The research survey on tile scheduling and caching (request priorities, concurrency, cancellation, retries, memory budgets, eviction) is written in docs/research/ with the chosen approach justified.
steps: Open the scheduling and caching survey in docs/research/
Verify it explains how CesiumJS, MapLibre GL JS, OpenLayers, Leaflet, loaders.gl, 3DTilesRendererJS, iTowns and Potree prioritize, throttle, cancel and cache tile requests, based on their code
Verify it lists stalled-loading, duplicate-request, memory-growth and flight-loading issues from their issue trackers, with links
Verify it summarizes how those projects test and benchmark loading
Verify it states the chosen scheduler and cache design and why, linking the ADR

features.description: The research survey on globe-to-flat transitions (projection morphing, anchor preservation, terrain scaling) is written in docs/research/ with the chosen approach justified.
steps: Open the globe-to-flat survey in docs/research/

Verify it explains how MapLibre GL JS interpolates between globe and Mercator, how CesiumJS morphs between 3D, 2D and Columbus view, and how deck.gl and OpenGlobus handle multiple projections, based on their code
Verify it lists sliding, jumping, precision and label issues during transitions from their issue trackers, with links
Verify it summarizes how those projects test transitions
Verify it states the chosen morph, anchor-point and terrain-scaling approach and why, linking the ADR

features.description: The research survey on camera control (anchored zoom, inertia, flights, collision, touch gestures) is written in docs/research/ with the chosen approach justified.
steps: Open the camera-control survey in docs/research/

Verify it explains how CesiumJS, MapLibre GL JS, OpenLayers, Leaflet, NASA WorldWind, iTowns and the three.js controls implement zoom, pan, rotate, tilt, inertia and flights, and covers van Wijk and Nuij's smooth zooming and panning
Verify it lists camera jumps, gesture conflicts, inertia and terrain-collision issues from their issue trackers, with links
Verify it summarizes how those projects test camera behavior
Verify it states the chosen camera and input design and why, linking the ADR

features.description: The research survey on GPU resource management and renderer backends (WebGPU, WebGL2 fallback, uploads, batching, state sorting, device loss) is written in docs/research/ with the chosen approach justified.
steps: Open the GPU and renderer survey in docs/research/

Verify it explains how three.js WebGPURenderer, Babylon.js, PlayCanvas, Filament, bgfx, Bevy, Godot, O3DE and CesiumJS manage buffers, textures, pipelines, uploads, draw-call batching and device or context loss
Verify it lists memory-leak, upload-stall, backend-inconsistency and device-loss issues from their issue trackers, with links
Verify it summarizes how those projects test rendering across backends
Verify it states whether three.js is adopted as the rendering base (and which pinned version) or why another option is better, linking the ADR

features.description: The research survey on worker usage (decoding, parsing, mesh generation, OffscreenCanvas, transferables, worker pools) is written in docs/research/ with the chosen approach justified.
steps: Open the worker survey in docs/research/
Verify it explains how MapLibre GL JS, CesiumJS, loaders.gl, deck.gl, 3DTilesRendererJS, Potree and OpenLayers distribute work to workers and whether they render from a worker with OffscreenCanvas
Verify it lists worker startup, transfer-cost, CSP and bundler-resolution issues from their issue trackers, with links
Verify it summarizes how those projects test and benchmark worker code
Verify it states the chosen worker architecture and why, linking the ADR

features.description: The research survey on rendering tests and benchmarks (render tests, visual regression, frame-time benchmarks, GPU-less CI) is written in docs/research/ with the chosen approach justified.
steps: Open the testing and benchmarks survey in docs/research/
Verify it explains how CesiumJS, MapLibre GL JS, three.js, Babylon.js, deck.gl and Filament run render tests, visual regression and performance benchmarks, including on CI machines without a GPU
Verify it lists flaky-test and cross-platform tolerance issues from their issue trackers, with links
Verify it states the chosen test tooling, image tolerances and benchmark method and why, linking the ADR

features.description: The monorepo contains every package from Architecture guidance (core, renderer, sources, layers, controls, offline, ui, vue, web-component, tools, playground) with lowercase names and the same predictable folder structure.
steps: List the workspaces and confirm all eleven packages exist with lowercase package names
Run the folder-structure check and confirm every package follows the same layout (package.json, src/, tests next to code, CLAUDE.md)
Rename a package folder in a scratch branch to break the layout and confirm the check fails
Run npm run build and confirm every package builds

features.description: Every library package builds to ES modules with TypeScript declaration files and an exports map that resolves types.
steps: Run npm run build
Inspect each library package's output and confirm ES module JavaScript plus .d.ts files
Confirm each package.json has type module and an exports map with types entries
Import the built packages from a Node ESM script and from a minimal Vite app and confirm both resolve
Compile a consumer file against the built declarations in strict mode and confirm zero type errors

features.description: All code is TypeScript in strict mode using ES modules, and the repository type check passes with zero errors.
steps: Confirm the shared tsconfig enables strict mode and every package extends it
Confirm every package.json declares type module
Run npm run typecheck and confirm it exits with code 0
Introduce an implicit any in a scratch file and confirm the type check fails

features.description: A formatter enforces one code style across the whole repository.
steps: Run the format check and confirm it passes
Misformat a source file in a scratch branch and confirm the format check fails
Run the format command and confirm the file is fixed and the check passes again

features.description: The linter forbids `any` and requires TSDoc on every public API.
steps: Run npm run lint and confirm it passes
Add an explicit any in a scratch file and confirm the lint fails
Export a public function without a TSDoc comment from a package entry point and confirm the lint fails
Confirm the lint runs in CI

features.description: A dead-code check fails on unused exports, unused files, unused dependencies and commented-out code.
steps: Run the dead-code check and confirm it passes
Add an unused exported function in a scratch branch and confirm the check fails
Add an unused dependency to a package.json and confirm the check fails
Add a block of commented-out code and confirm the check fails

features.description: Performance-critical code lives in clearly marked hot-path modules that document the reason and the benchmark that justifies the trade-off.
steps: Confirm the hot-path marking convention is documented in CLAUDE.md
Run the hot-path check and confirm every marked module names its reason and an existing benchmark
Mark a module as hot path without a benchmark reference in a scratch branch and confirm the check fails

features.section: Working method for a multi-session build
features.description: Claude Code hooks run the formatter, linter and type check automatically on every change.
steps: Open the project Claude Code settings and confirm hooks for format, lint and type check
In a Claude Code session, edit a file so that it contains a lint error and confirm the hook reports it immediately
Edit a file with formatting problems and confirm the hook formats it
Confirm CI runs the same checks

features.section: Working method for a multi-session build
features.description: A concise root CLAUDE.md and a CLAUDE.md per package document commands, conventions that differ from defaults, testing, architecture decisions and gotchas.
steps: Open the root CLAUDE.md and confirm it is short (at most 80 lines) and covers commands, conventions, testing, architecture decision pointers and gotchas
Confirm it states that code, comments, documentation and commit messages are in English and that names carry units where ambiguous (meters, degrees, radians, pixels)
Confirm every package has its own CLAUDE.md
Run every command listed in the CLAUDE.md files and confirm each one works
Confirm the commit messages in git history are in English

features.description: Unit tests live next to the code they test and all of them run with one command.
steps: Run npm test and confirm the tests of every package run and pass
Confirm test files sit next to the modules they test
Add a failing assertion in a scratch branch and confirm npm test exits with a non-zero code

features.description: Line coverage of core logic is enforced at 90% or more in CI.
steps: Run the coverage command and confirm it produces a coverage report
Confirm the configured threshold for core logic is at least 90% of lines
Remove tests in a scratch branch so coverage drops below the threshold and confirm the command fails
Confirm CI runs the coverage check

features.description: CI runs type check, lint, format check, unit tests, API documentation build and license audit on every push and pull request, and is green on the main branch.
steps: Open the CI workflow definition and confirm each job: type check, lint, format check, unit tests with coverage, API documentation build, license audit
Push a commit and confirm every job runs and passes
Push a commit with a type error in a scratch branch and confirm CI fails
Confirm the latest CI run on the main branch is green

features.description: A license audit fails the build when any shipped dependency has a license outside the permissive allowlist (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, OFL for fonts).
steps: Run the license audit and confirm it passes
Confirm the allowlist contains only MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC and OFL (fonts only)
Add a GPL-licensed dependency in a scratch branch and confirm the audit fails
Add an LGPL or AGPL dependency in a scratch branch and confirm the audit fails
Confirm CI runs the audit

features.description: A third-party notices file is generated from the shipped dependency tree and kept up to date.
steps: Run the notices generator and confirm it writes the third-party notices file
Confirm the file lists every production dependency with its license text
Run the generator twice and confirm the output is identical
Add a dependency in a scratch branch without regenerating and confirm CI reports the file as stale

features.description: A documentation site scaffold builds and serves the guides and the API reference generated from the types.
steps: Run the documentation build and confirm it succeeds
Serve the site and open it in a browser
Confirm the API reference pages are generated from the TypeScript types of every package
Confirm CI builds the documentation

features.description: The playground app starts with one command and loads without console errors.
steps: Run npm run dev and open http://localhost:5173/
With Playwright, load the page and confirm the app container and canvas are present
Confirm no console errors or unhandled promise rejections are logged
Run npm run test:e2e and confirm the playground smoke test passes

features.description: A debug overlay skeleton opens with ?debug=1 and shows the live frame time and frame rate.
steps: Open http://localhost:5173/?debug=1
Confirm the debug overlay is visible and shows frame time and frame rate values that update
Open the playground without ?debug=1 and confirm no overlay is shown and no overlay code is loaded
Cover it with a Playwright test

features.description: An automated benchmark harness measures CPU and GPU frame time and memory per scenario and fails when a configured budget is broken.
steps: Run the benchmark command and confirm it runs the configured scenarios in a real browser
Confirm it records CPU frame time and JS heap per scenario, plus GPU frame time and GPU memory where the active backend exposes them (reported as unavailable before the renderer exists)
Confirm frame-time budgets are defined per feature and memory budgets per package (measured in the scenarios that exercise each package) in a versioned configuration file
Set an unachievable budget in a scratch branch and confirm the benchmark command fails
Confirm results are written as machine-readable files that can be compared over time

features.description: Each package has a bundle-size budget enforced in CI, and optional modules are lazily loaded to keep the initial bundle small.
steps: Run the bundle-size check and confirm it reports the minified and compressed size of each package entry
Confirm each package has a budget in configuration
Add a large dependency to a package in a scratch branch and confirm the check fails
Load the playground and confirm optional modules (for example the debug overlay) are fetched only when used

features.description: Importing any package under server-side rendering (Node, no window, document or GPU) succeeds and touches no browser API at import time.
steps: Run the SSR import test that imports every package entry point in Node with window, document and navigator undefined
Confirm all imports succeed
Confirm, through guarded globals that throw on access, that no browser or GPU API is touched during import
Add a top-level document access to a module in a scratch branch and confirm the test fails
Confirm CI runs the test

features.description: The core and every non-adapter package depend on no framework (Vue, Nuxt, React), and integrations live only in separate adapter packages.
steps: Run the dependency-rule check and confirm it passes
Confirm the rules forbid framework imports and dependencies outside the vue and web-component adapter packages
Add a vue import to the core package in a scratch branch and confirm the check fails
Confirm CI runs the check

features.description: Packages are side-effect-free and tree-shakeable: importing one symbol bundles only the modules it needs.
steps: Confirm every library package.json declares sideEffects false or lists its only side-effectful files
Build a fixture app that imports a single small function from the core package
Inspect the bundle and confirm unrelated modules (renderer, sources, layers) are absent
Run this check in CI

features.description: The code lives in a private GitHub repository named VibeGlobeEngine, fully separate from Vireox Cube: it contains no Cube code, submodule or dependency.
steps: Query the repository through the GitHub API and confirm it is private and named VibeGlobeEngine (case-insensitive)
Confirm the repository has no git submodules referring to Cube
Run the dependency-rule check and confirm no package depends on or refers to Cube
Search the source tree and confirm it contains no Cube code (PLAN.md and docs may name Cube as the first consumer)

features.section: Working method for a multi-session build
features.description: A guard fails when tests are deleted, skipped or focused, or when coverage thresholds, visual-test tolerances or budgets are loosened, unless the change records its justification in the test-changes log.
steps: Run the test guard against the base revision and confirm it passes
In a scratch branch delete a test case and confirm the guard fails; record the deletion with its reason in the test-changes log and confirm the guard passes
Add .skip or .only to a test and confirm the lint fails
Lower the coverage threshold or loosen a budget in a scratch branch and confirm the guard fails
Confirm CI runs the guard

features.description: Lint rules cap function length and module size, with hot-path modules exempted.
steps: Run npm run lint and confirm the function-length and module-size rules are active
Add an over-long function and an over-long module in a scratch branch and confirm the lint fails
Confirm *.hot.ts modules are exempt from these two rules

features.description: The repository is SimoneRecchia/VibeGlobe on GitHub, under the owner's personal account and fully separate from Vireox Cube, and the project is named VibeGlobe everywhere: package metadata, documentation, code identifiers, the `<vibe-globe>` Web Component tag and the VIBEGLOBE_ environment-variable prefix.
steps: Query the repository through the GitHub API and confirm its full name is SimoneRecchia/VibeGlobe (case-insensitive) and the git remote of the working copy points to it

Search the tracked files case-insensitively for VibeGlobeEngine and for vge used as a prefix (VGE_, vge-, vge:, vgePlayground) and confirm the only matches are frozen feature-list text and the documents that record the rename (ADR 0015, ADR 0016, docs/feature-changes.md, docs/open-questions.md, docs/test-changes.md, progress.md)

Confirm the root package is named vibeglobe, every library uses the @vibeglobe/ scope, the Web Component tag is <vibe-globe>, and init.sh, the Playwright configuration, the benchmark runner and CI read VIBEGLOBE_ variables
Confirm the repository has no git submodule referring to Cube and the dependency-rule check finds no package depending on or referring to Cube
Run ./init.sh from a fresh clone and confirm it passes

features.description: VibeGlobe is licensed under the PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0: LICENSE.md holds the official text with the owner's required notice, every package.json declares PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0, the README explains free noncommercial use and how to request a commercial license, and every shipped dependency's license allows distribution under these terms.
steps: Compare LICENSE.md with the official PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 text from the PolyForm Project and confirm it is identical apart from the leading Required Notice line naming the owner

Run npm run check and confirm it requires the SPDX identifier PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0 in the root, library and app package.json files; remove the field from one package in a scratch branch and confirm the check fails
Open the README licensing section and confirm it states that noncommercial use is free, that any commercial use including resale needs a commercial license from the owner, and how to request one

Run the license audit and confirm every shipped third-party package is under a license in the permissive allowlist, and that ADR 0015 explains why each allowlisted license permits distribution inside a PolyForm Noncommercial project

features.description: The repository has a contributing guide, a contributor license agreement that lets the owner offer external contributions under both the noncommercial and the commercial licenses, a security policy, a code of conduct, issue templates and a pull request template that asks for the agreement.
steps: Open CONTRIBUTING.md and confirm it requires external contributors to accept CLA.md and states the repository rules (feature list, tests, bugs, licenses, ADRs) and how to submit

Open CLA.md and confirm contributors keep their copyright and grant copyright and patent licenses that allow distribution under PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 and under commercial licenses, and that it explains how to accept
Open SECURITY.md and CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and confirm supported versions, a private reporting channel, a response time and the enforcement contact

Open .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ and .github/pull_request_template.md and confirm bug, feature, question and commercial-license templates, a security link instead of blank issues, and the CLA acceptance line
Confirm the README links to the licensing section, the contributing guide, the security policy and the code of conduct

features.description: CI saves minutes on GitHub-hosted runners without a GPU: every push and every pull request from a fork runs one fast job with the type check, lint, format check, repository checks and guards, unit tests with coverage, license audit, API documentation build and bundle-size checks, while pushes to main, a nightly schedule and manual runs add the end-to-end tests and the recorded benchmarks.
steps: Open the CI workflow and confirm its triggers and the conditions of each job match the description
Push a branch and confirm its run contains only the fast job, every listed check runs, and a newer push cancels the older run
Confirm a pull request from the same repository shows the fast job of its head commit and starts no duplicate run of the checks
Confirm the latest run on main and the latest nightly run contain the fast, end-to-end and benchmark jobs and are green

features.description: Milestone 1 acceptance: the core research survey is written, CI is green and the playground runs.
steps: Confirm every M1 research survey entry in feature_list.json passes
Confirm the latest CI run on the main branch is green
Run ./init.sh from a fresh clone and confirm the playground starts and the Playwright smoke test passes
Confirm no known bug remains open for this milestone
A fresh-context reviewer checks the milestone against PLAN.md and its acceptance criteria and reports no correctness or requirement gaps

features.description: Geodetic and Earth-centered (ECEF) coordinates convert both ways on the WGS84 ellipsoid with sub-millimeter round-trip error everywhere, including the poles.
steps: Run the unit tests for geodetic to ECEF and ECEF to geodetic conversion
Confirm results match reference values from an independent geodesy source to within 1 mm
Run property-based tests with random positions, heights from -12 km to +40,000 km and latitudes up to exactly ±90°, and confirm round trips stay within 1 mm
Confirm the WGS84 constants (semi-major axis 6378137 m, flattening 1/298.257223563) are the only ellipsoid used

features.description: Every position the public API accepts or returns is WGS84 geodetic (longitude and latitude in degrees, height in meters above the ellipsoid), whatever the display projection.
steps: Inspect the public types and confirm positions are typed WGS84 geodetic values with units in their names or documentation
In the playground, read the camera position in the globe phase and confirm it is WGS84 degrees and meters
Run the API unit tests that pass positions in and out and confirm no projected coordinates leak through the public API

features.description: Local east-north-up frames and heading, pitch and roll transforms are correct at any point on the ellipsoid.
steps: Run the unit tests for east-north-up frames and heading/pitch/roll to rotation conversions
Confirm the axes are orthonormal and point east, north and up against reference values
Run property-based tests for round trips and continuity at the poles and across the antimeridian

features.description: Web Mercator and geographic (plate carrée) projections convert both ways, are continuous across the antimeridian and clamp Web Mercator at about ±85.0511° latitude.
steps: Run the projection unit tests against reference values
Run property-based round-trip tests for both projections
Confirm longitudes either side of ±180° map to adjacent projected positions with correct wrapping
Confirm latitudes beyond the Web Mercator limit are clamped without NaN or infinity

features.description: Property-based tests cover every math and geodesy module, run in CI with a reproducible seed, and check round trips, symmetry and continuity at the poles and the antimeridian.
steps: Run npm test and confirm property-based suites run for every math and geodesy module
Confirm each suite checks round trips, symmetry and continuity at the poles and the antimeridian
Confirm a failure prints the seed and the shrunk counterexample, and re-running with that seed reproduces it
Confirm CI runs the suites

features.description: The camera model stores its position in double precision with heading, tilt and roll, and produces view and projection matrices and a frustum that match reference values.
steps: Run the camera unit tests for view matrix, projection matrix and frustum planes
Place the camera at known positions (orbit, 1 km, 1 m above ground) with known heading and tilt and confirm the matrices against reference values
Confirm the camera state API exposes position, heading, tilt and roll with units in their names

features.description: A screen point is converted to the WGS84 position it shows on the globe (ray-ellipsoid intersection), and points off the globe return no position.
steps: Run unit tests that cast rays through screen pixels and intersect the ellipsoid
In the playground, move the pointer over known features of the pinned imagery and confirm the reported coordinates within one pixel's ground size
Move the pointer over empty space beside the globe and confirm no position is reported and no error occurs

features.description: The engine exposes a typed public API: a typed configuration object, typed events and promise-based methods.
steps: Create an engine instance in a TypeScript consumer with typed options and confirm invalid option types fail to compile
Subscribe to typed events (for example frame rendered, backend ready, error) and confirm payload types
Confirm asynchronous operations return promises
Confirm the public API is generated into the API reference with TSDoc

features.description: Engine configuration and coordinate inputs are validated where they enter the engine, and invalid values produce typed errors instead of crashes or a blank view.
steps: Run unit tests passing invalid options (wrong types, NaN, out-of-range latitudes, negative sizes) and confirm typed, descriptive errors
Run a fuzz test over the configuration parser with random inputs and confirm it never throws an untyped error or hangs
In the playground, apply an invalid camera position at runtime and confirm the view stays rendered and an error event is emitted

features.description: Rendering goes through the engine's own renderer interface; the rendering library chosen in the renderer ADR (three.js unless the ADR justifies another option) is pinned to an exact version and used only inside the renderer package.
steps: Confirm the renderer package.json pins the chosen rendering library to an exact version
Run the dependency-rule check and confirm no package other than renderer imports that library
Confirm all globe logic (tiles, levels of detail, precision, camera) lives outside the renderer package
Add an import of the rendering library to the core package in a scratch branch and confirm the check fails

features.description: Tile meshes bypass the rendering library's automatic matrix updates and frustum culling (the engine culls), and texture uploads happen only when the engine schedules them.
steps: Run renderer unit tests confirming tile objects have automatic matrix updates and frustum culling disabled
Instrument the renderer in the playground and confirm per-frame matrix updates are not performed for unchanged tiles
Confirm textures upload only when the engine's upload scheduler releases them, by counting uploads per frame in a Playwright test

features.description: On a browser with WebGPU, the engine renders with the WebGPU backend by default.
steps: Open the playground in Chrome with WebGPU available
Confirm the engine reports webgpu as the active backend in its API and the debug overlay
Capture a screenshot and confirm the globe is rendered

features.description: When WebGPU is unavailable or fails to initialize, the engine falls back automatically to WebGL2 with the same API and rendering.
steps: Open the playground in a browser without WebGPU, and again with navigator.gpu removed by a Playwright init script
Simulate a failed adapter request and confirm the engine still starts
Confirm the active backend is webgl2 and the globe renders
Open http://localhost:5173/?backend=webgl2 and confirm the backend can also be forced

features.description: On a device with neither WebGPU nor WebGL2, the engine reports a clear typed error and the host page keeps working.
steps: Open the playground with WebGPU and WebGL2 both disabled by a Playwright init script
Confirm the engine emits a typed unsupported-device error with a human-readable message
Confirm the page does not crash and no unhandled exception is logged

features.description: Capability detection reports the active backend, GPU limits and memory hints through the API and the debug overlay.
steps: Open http://localhost:5173/?debug=1 on each backend
Confirm the overlay shows the active backend, key GPU limits (maximum texture size, maximum anisotropy, compressed texture formats) and memory hints
Read the same values through the public capabilities API in a Playwright test

features.description: Geometry shows no vertex jitter at street level despite 32-bit GPU floats.
steps: Run scenario ?scenario=street-level-jitter: camera about 1 m above the ground at several places worldwide, moving and rotating slowly
Record every frame and track reference vertices in screen space
Confirm the residual screen-space motion not explained by camera movement stays below 0.1 px
Repeat on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: Near and far geometry in the same view show no z-fighting.

Confirm surfaces at a few centimeters of separation resolve in the correct order across the depth range

features.description: A plain globe with pinned low-resolution imagery renders completely from orbit, with no black or empty areas on the Earth.

features.description: Dragging the globe with the mouse keeps the grabbed geographic point under the cursor.

Confirm after each move that the point under the cursor is the grabbed point, within one pixel
Confirm dragging near the globe edge and over a pole causes no jump

features.description: Wheel zoom is anchored at the cursor and reaches from orbit down to about 1 m above the ground.
steps: In the playground, with Playwright scroll the wheel over a known point repeatedly
Confirm the geographic point under the cursor stays under the cursor after each step, within one pixel
Continue until the camera is about 1 m above the ground and confirm the camera never goes below the ellipsoid surface
Zoom back out to orbit and confirm the globe is complete

features.description: The engine renders continuously while anything moves, animates or loads, and stops drawing when nothing changes.
steps: Open the playground and leave it idle after loading
Confirm with the frame counter that no frames are rendered while idle
Drag the globe and confirm frames render during the movement and stop shortly after it ends
Change a setting that alters the image (for example layer opacity) and confirm rendering starts on the next frame and stops within a few frames after the last visible change

features.description: Rendering is throttled while the tab is hidden and resumes immediately when it becomes visible.

Hide the page (visibility hidden) with Playwright and confirm no frames are drawn
Show the page again and confirm rendering resumes on the next frame with no stale or blank frame

features.description: The per-frame loop allocates no garbage, so garbage collection never causes a stutter.

Sample heap allocations during the steady state and confirm the frame loop allocates zero bytes per frame
Confirm no garbage-collection pause appears in the recorded trace during the steady state

features.description: Rendering from a worker with OffscreenCanvas is evaluated with measurements, and the outcome is recorded in an ADR.

Confirm it records frame-time and input-latency measurements for main-thread and worker rendering in the supported browsers
Confirm it states the decision and, if adopted, which browsers use it and how the fallback works

features.description: When the WebGPU device is lost, the engine recovers and renders again without reloading the page.
steps: Open the playground on the WebGPU backend

Confirm the engine emits a device-lost event, recreates the device and its GPU resources, and renders a complete view again
Confirm the camera, layers and settings are preserved

features.description: When the WebGL2 context is lost, the engine recovers and renders again without reloading the page.

Force context loss with WEBGL_lose_context and restore it
Confirm the engine emits context-lost and restored events and renders a complete view again
Confirm the camera, layers and settings are preserved

features.description: destroy() frees GPU memory, RAM, workers and event listeners, leaving nothing behind.
steps: Create an engine in the playground, navigate, then call destroy()
Confirm the engine's GPU resource counters reach zero and the device or context is released
Confirm all workers are terminated and all DOM and window event listeners are removed
Confirm calling API methods after destroy() throws a typed error instead of crashing

features.description: Several engine instances run independently on the same page.

Destroy one and confirm the other keeps rendering correctly

features.description: Resizing the container renders the next frame at the new size with the correct aspect ratio and no stretched or blank frame.

Confirm the globe stays centered on the same geographic point with the correct aspect ratio

Confirm results are saved in the documented location with the device, OS, browser and GPU recorded

features.description: Geodesic path length and polygon area on the WGS84 ellipsoid are computed with Karney's algorithms, including polygons around a pole or across the antimeridian.

Run property-based tests verifying area is invariant to vertex order rotation and sign follows orientation

features.description: The renderer's three.js cost is measured after tree-shaking, the initial-JavaScript byte budget is set from that measurement in quality/budgets.json, and the CI size check fails on any regression beyond it; time to first frame (at most 1 s from a LAN server) is the binding target, with no separate lightweight first-frame path.

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Imagery is organized in quadtree pyramids for Web Mercator and geographic tiling schemes, with correct tile keys, bounds, parents and children.
steps: Run the tiling unit tests for both schemes

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: A parent tile is never discarded before all the children needed to replace it are ready.
steps: Serve fixture tiles with Playwright route interception and delay one child of a refining tile

features.description: A missing tile is always covered by its best available ancestor, upsampled, so no black area ever appears.
steps: Serve fixture tiles and make some levels fail or never arrive
Zoom deep into the affected area and record every frame
Confirm the area shows the upsampled best available ancestor and zero black or background pixels
Confirm the debug overlay marks the area as drawn from an ancestor

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: The pinned base levels load at startup and are never evicted, so a complete picture is always available.
steps: Start the playground and confirm the pinned levels finish loading before refinement begins
Set a very small memory budget and navigate widely until eviction occurs
Confirm pinned tiles are never evicted and zooming out to the globe immediately shows complete imagery with no new request for pinned tiles

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Once the base is visible, detail refines progressively toward the level the view needs.
steps: Throttle the fixture tile server and jump to a city-level view
Record frames and the requested tile levels over time
Confirm the view first shows the base, then intermediate levels, then the target level, and every frame is complete

features.description: Frustum culling skips tiles outside the view.
steps: Run culling unit tests with known frustums and tile bounds
In the playground, confirm through the debug overlay that no tile outside the view is selected or drawn
Rotate quickly and confirm no visible tile is wrongly culled (zero empty pixels at the screen edges)

features.description: Horizon culling skips tiles hidden behind the curve of the Earth.
steps: Run horizon-culling unit tests for points and tile bounding volumes at several altitudes
In the playground at a low oblique view, confirm tiles beyond the horizon are not selected or requested
Confirm no tile visible near the horizon is wrongly culled (zero empty pixels below the horizon line)

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Requests are scheduled by priority: screen center first, coarse before fine, visible before prefetch.
steps: Run the scheduler unit tests with mixed priorities
In the playground, record the order of tile requests after a jump to a new view
Confirm center tiles precede edge tiles, coarser levels precede finer ones, and visible tiles precede prefetch tiles

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Concurrent requests are limited per host.
steps: Configure a per-host limit and serve fixture tiles from two hosts
Trigger a large refinement and record in-flight requests per host over time
Confirm in-flight requests to each host never exceed its limit and both hosts are used in parallel

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Requests that are no longer needed are cancelled, which keeps flights and fast pans responsive.
steps: Throttle the fixture server and pan quickly across many tiles
Confirm requests for tiles that left the view before arriving are aborted
Run a long scripted camera path from Milan to Tokyo (?scenario=path-milan-tokyo) and confirm requests for tiles passed along the path are cancelled
Confirm new visible tiles load without waiting for stale requests

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Failed tile requests are retried with backoff and a bounded number of attempts.
steps: Make the fixture server return HTTP 503 or drop the connection for some tiles a fixed number of times
Confirm those tiles are retried with increasing delays and eventually load
Make a tile fail permanently and confirm retries stop after the configured maximum and the parent stays drawn

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Tile requests time out after a configured duration instead of hanging.
steps: Make the fixture server never respond for some tiles
Confirm those requests are aborted after the configured timeout and handled by the retry policy
Confirm the concurrency slots are freed and other tiles keep loading

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: An HTTP 404 or an out-of-coverage tile means no data: the engine stays on the parent and never retries endlessly.
steps: Make the fixture server return 404 for an area at deep levels
Zoom into the area and confirm the parent stays drawn, each missing tile is requested once and no retries follow
Pan away and back and confirm the known-missing tiles are not requested again

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Sources declare their coverage, and tiles outside it are never requested.
steps: Configure a fixture source covering only one region and a zoom range
Navigate inside and outside the region and beyond the zoom range
Confirm no request is made for tiles outside the declared coverage or zoom range, and the parent is drawn there

features.description: The same tile is never downloaded twice: concurrent needs for one tile share a single request, and loaded tiles are reused from cache.
steps: Make two selection passes want the same tile at the same time within one layer, then navigate
Record all network requests and confirm each tile URL is requested at most once
Pan away and back within the cache budget and confirm no repeated request

features.description: Tile loading uses HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 multiplexing and compressed responses efficiently.
steps: Serve fixture tiles from an HTTP/2 server with compression enabled
Confirm in the browser network log that tile requests share connections per host
Confirm compressed responses (for example gzip or brotli for vector and terrain data) are accepted and decoded

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Recently used tiles stay in a RAM cache and are reused without new requests after they leave the screen.
steps: Unit test the RAM cache: hits, misses and reuse after tiles leave the view
Navigate to a view, pan away, then return
Confirm the returning tiles are served from the RAM cache with no new request
Confirm the debug overlay counts cache hits for them

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: GPU and RAM memory budgets are never exceeded, and least-recently-used tiles are evicted first while visible tiles are never evicted.
steps: Unit test budget accounting and least-recently-used eviction order, including pinned and visible tiles
Configure small GPU and RAM budgets in the playground
Navigate widely and record memory use over time
Confirm memory use never exceeds the budgets
Confirm the evicted tiles are the least recently used and no tile on screen is ever evicted

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Tile decoding runs in workers, keeping the main thread free.
steps: Stream imagery heavily in the playground while recording a performance trace
Confirm image decoding happens in worker threads
Confirm no main-thread task longer than the per-frame budget is caused by decoding

features.description: The engine runs under a strict Content Security Policy: no eval or dynamic code generation, and workers and other assets load as separate files from configurable URLs.
steps: Serve the playground with a strict CSP header (no unsafe-eval, worker-src limited to the configured asset origin)
Confirm the engine starts, streams imagery and logs no CSP violation
Configure a different asset base URL and confirm workers and assets load from it
Search the built bundles and confirm no eval, new Function or blob-generated code

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: GPU uploads and other expensive work are spread across frames within a per-frame budget, so no single frame stutters.
steps: Trigger a burst of tile arrivals (jump to a new view with a fast fixture server)
Record per-frame upload time and CPU time
Confirm no frame exceeds the per-frame upload budget and the total frame budget defined in docs/plan
Confirm all uploads complete within a bounded number of frames

features.description: Each tile texture is uploaded to the GPU once while it stays resident; there are no redundant uploads.
steps: Count texture uploads per tile during navigation that keeps tiles resident
Confirm each resident tile is uploaded exactly once
Confirm re-showing a cached tile triggers no upload

features.description: Tile rendering uses few draw calls and state changes through batching, instancing, texture arrays or atlases and state sorting.
steps: Open each canonical view with the debug overlay
Record draw calls and pipeline or state changes per frame
Confirm both stay within the budgets defined in docs/plan and do not grow linearly with the number of visible tiles beyond the documented batching factor

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: GPU-compressed textures (KTX2/Basis) are used where supported to reduce memory and upload time, with a fallback where they are not.
steps: Serve a KTX2 fixture imagery source
On a device supporting a compressed format, confirm tiles upload in compressed form and GPU memory per tile drops versus uncompressed
On a device or backend without support, confirm tiles transcode to a supported format and render correctly
Record the memory and upload-time measurements in the ADR

features.description: Imagery level changes cross-fade, so no tile pops in.
steps: Run ?scenario=zoom-orbit-to-street and record every frame
Measure frame-to-frame differences at tile refinement events
Confirm each refinement changes pixels gradually over the configured cross-fade duration with no single-frame jump above the popping threshold
Repeat on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: Tile edges show no filtering lines or seams at any zoom or tilt.
steps: Use a fixture source with strongly contrasting colors at tile borders
Capture screenshots at fractional zoom levels, tilted views and high pixel density
Analyze pixels along tile boundaries and confirm no line or seam differs from the neighboring content beyond tolerance
Repeat on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: Imagery uses mipmaps, so minified tiles show no aliasing or shimmer.
steps: Use a high-frequency fixture pattern and view it minified and tilted
Record frames while moving slowly
Confirm frame differencing shows no shimmer beyond tolerance and screenshots match the baseline

features.description: Imagery is displayed in the correct color space, with colors matching the source.
steps: Use a fixture tile with known sRGB color patches
Capture a screenshot of the patches at native resolution
Confirm each patch's displayed color matches the source within tolerance on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: High-DPI screens are supported with a resolution scale setting that trades sharpness for performance.
steps: Open the playground at device pixel ratio 2 with resolution scale 1 and confirm the canvas renders at full device resolution
Set resolution scale to 0.5 at runtime and confirm the backing size halves without a blank frame
Confirm tile selection uses the effective pixel size so imagery stays sharp at scale 1

features.description: The poles show no gap beyond the Web Mercator latitude limit: polar caps cover them.
steps: Run ?scenario=pole-orbit circling both poles at several altitudes
Record every frame and confirm zero black or background pixels inside the globe's silhouette
Confirm the cap joins the imagery at about ±85° without a visible seam

features.description: The antimeridian shows no gap or seam on the globe.

features.description: Corrupted tiles are handled gracefully: the parent stays drawn and the engine never crashes or blanks the view.
steps: Make the fixture server return truncated, random-byte and wrong-content-type responses for some tiles
Navigate across the affected area and record every frame
Confirm the parent stays drawn, an error is logged or emitted, and no frame has black or empty pixels

features.description: Slow servers never freeze or blank the view: the camera stays fluid and ancestors cover pending tiles.
steps: Throttle the fixture server to very high latency and low bandwidth
Navigate continuously and record frames and frame times
Confirm frame times stay within budget and no frame has black or empty pixels

features.description: Fuzz tests feed random and mutated bytes to every imagery decoder, which never crashes, hangs or leaks.
steps: Run the imagery decoder fuzz suite for the configured number of iterations
Confirm every input yields either a decoded tile or a typed error, never an uncaught exception or hang
Confirm worker memory stays flat across the run

features.description: The first complete frame from a local or LAN base appears within 1 s.
steps: Serve the pinned base from a local HTTP server
Run the start-up benchmark on the reference desktop and record time from engine creation to the first frame with complete imagery
Confirm it is at most 1 s and record the result

features.description: The debug overlay shows tile boundaries, levels, screen-space error and the source of each tile.
steps: Open http://localhost:5173/?debug=1 and enable the tile view
Confirm tile boundaries are outlined and each tile is labeled with its level, screen-space error and source
Confirm tiles drawn from an ancestor are distinguishable
Confirm turning the overlay off restores the unmodified view

features.description: The debug overlay shows cache hits and misses, requests in flight, GPU and RAM memory, frame time and frame rate.
steps: Open http://localhost:5173/?debug=1 and navigate
Confirm the overlay shows cache hits and misses, requests in flight, GPU memory, RAM memory, frame time and frame rate

features.description: Timing marks for engine phases are visible in the browser's performance tools.
steps: Record a performance trace while navigating
Confirm named marks and measures for frame phases (update, selection, scheduling, upload, render) appear in the trace
Confirm marks are disabled by default or have no measurable cost when disabled

features.description: A compact performance HUD shows frame time, frame rate and the main per-frame costs.
steps: Enable the performance HUD in the playground
Confirm it shows frame time, frame rate and per-phase costs, updating live
Confirm enabling the HUD does not change frame time beyond the documented overhead

features.description: Engine logging supports levels and can be configured at runtime.
steps: Set the log level to debug, info, warn, error and silent in turn
Confirm only messages at or above the level are emitted
Confirm a custom log sink receives the messages instead of the console

features.description: Event traces for tiles, requests and camera movement can be recorded and exported.
steps: Enable tracing and run a short navigation
Export the trace and confirm it contains tile state changes, request start, end, cancel and failure events, and camera movement events with timestamps
Confirm tracing has no measurable cost when disabled

features.description: Scenario tests run scripted camera paths, record frames and automatically detect black or background pixels and holes.
steps: Run the scenario test suite of scripted camera paths (globe to street zoom, long path, fast pans, rotations, tilt changes) against the fixture tile server
Confirm every frame is recorded and analyzed for black or background pixels inside the Earth's area
Inject a missing-tile bug in a scratch branch and confirm the suite fails and reports the frame
Confirm the suite runs on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: Temporal glitch detection analyzes recorded frames to catch popping, flicker, seams and z-fighting shimmer.
steps: Run the temporal analysis over recorded scenario frames
Inject a pop (disable cross-fade), a flicker (alternate two tile levels) and a seam in a scratch branch and confirm each is detected
Confirm the unmodified engine passes all detectors

features.description: Streaming benchmarks record frame-time distribution, time to first frame, tiles loaded, requests and memory, and track them over time.
steps: Run the streaming benchmark scenarios
Confirm results include frame-time percentiles, time to first frame, tile and request counts, and memory
Confirm results are stored with the commit id and compared against the previous run, flagging regressions

features.description: Milestone 3 acceptance: scripted zoom and pan scenarios show zero black pixels and no popping.
steps: Run the scripted zoom and pan scenarios on WebGPU and record every frame
Confirm zero black or background pixels after the base has loaded
Confirm the temporal detectors find no popping, flicker or seams

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Terrain tiles form their own quadtree pyramid and are selected by screen-space error computed from the terrain source's geometric error per level.
steps: Run the Vitest suite for terrain tile selection against a fixture terrain source that declares a geometric error per level
For scripted camera positions, assert the selected terrain tile set matches the expected set and every selected tile's screen-space error is at or below the configured maximum
Open `http://localhost:5173/?scenario=terrain-alps&debug=1` and drive a zoom from 50 km to 500 m altitude with Playwright
Assert from the debug overlay data that terrain levels increase toward the camera and that no tile is refined beyond the source's maximum level

features.description: The quantized-mesh terrain adapter decodes tiles (header, zig-zag delta-encoded vertices, high-water-mark indices in 16 and 32 bits, edge index lists, oct-encoded normals and water-mask extensions), gzip-compressed or not.
steps: Decode a set of fixture .terrain tiles covering every variant (with and without extensions, 16- and 32-bit indices, gzip and uncompressed) in a Vitest suite
Assert decoded vertex positions, heights, triangle indices, edge index lists and normals equal the reference values stored with the fixtures

Navigate the playground over available and unavailable areas with Playwright while recording every network request
Assert zero requests for tiles outside the declared availability and that those areas render with the best available ancestor terrain
Assert extensions are requested (Accept header) only when layer.json declares them

Open `?scenario=terrain-terrarium` with the fixtures on both backends and capture screenshots
Assert the pixel diff against the baselines is within the visual tolerance

features.description: The Terrain-RGB heightmap adapter decodes 256- and 512-pixel tiles with height = −10000 + (R × 65536 + G × 256 + B) × 0.1 meters.
steps: Decode fixture Terrain-RGB tiles of 256 and 512 pixels in a Vitest suite
Assert sampled heights equal the encoding formula to the encoding's 0.1 m resolution, including synthetic tiles at the minimum and maximum encodable heights
Open `?scenario=terrain-rgb` with the fixtures on both backends and capture screenshots
Assert the pixel diff against the baselines is within the visual tolerance

features.description: Every terrain decoder (quantized-mesh, Terrarium, Terrain-RGB) survives fuzzed input: malformed, truncated or random bytes never crash the engine or blank the view, and the affected tile falls back to its ancestor.
steps: Run the terrain decoder fuzz suite for the configured iteration budget with mutated fixtures and random bytes
Assert every input either decodes or returns a typed decode error, with no exception escaping, no hang beyond the timeout and no unbounded allocation
Serve corrupted terrain tiles in the playground and record frames with a sentinel clear color on both backends
Assert zero sentinel pixels and that the corrupted tiles are covered by their best available ancestor

features.description: Any other elevation encoding can be added through the public terrain adapter interface (for example a custom RGB formula or raw float32 tiles) without changing the engine.

Load both in the playground through the public API on both backends
Assert the rendered relief and elevation queries match the fixture heights within the encodings' precision
Assert the test adapters import nothing beyond the published package entry points

features.description: Terrain sources declare their vertical datum, and geoid-referenced heights (for example EGM2008, used by Copernicus DEM) are converted to WGS84 ellipsoidal heights before meshing and elevation queries.
steps: Unit test the geoid-to-ellipsoid conversion at reference points against published geoid undulation values within the documented tolerance
Load the same fixture area once as an ellipsoid-referenced source and once as a geoid-referenced source
Assert elevation queries and rendered vertex positions agree between the two within tolerance

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Terrain decoding and mesh generation (including heightmap triangulation with a bounded geometric error) run in workers, and terrain mesh uploads respect the per-frame upload budget, so terrain streaming causes no main-thread stutter.
steps: Unit test heightmap triangulation: the maximum vertical error between the mesh and the source heights is at or below the configured threshold at every sample
Open `?scenario=terrain-alps` and record a performance trace with Playwright during a scripted zoom-in
Assert decoding and mesh generation run only on worker threads and the main-thread time attributable to terrain per frame stays within the terrain CPU budget in docs/plan

features.description: Rendered terrain relief matches the source heights: every vertex is placed at its WGS84 ellipsoidal height along the ellipsoid normal.
steps: Unit test mesh generation: every vertex position equals the geodetic-to-ECEF conversion of its longitude, latitude and height within 1 mm
Render a fixture containing an analytic synthetic mountain on both backends and compare screenshots against analytically generated baselines
Read back depth at selected pixels and assert reconstructed positions match the analytic surface within the depth-precision tolerance

features.description: Terrain meshes use relative-to-center coordinates (or an equivalent precision technique), so terrain vertices show no jitter at street level.
steps: Open `?scenario=terrain-street-level` with the camera 2 m above steep terrain on both backends
Record every frame during a slow scripted orbit and during a static hold
Assert by frame differencing that terrain features move only by the expected camera motion and the static hold shows zero vertex oscillation above the jitter threshold

features.description: Cracks between adjacent terrain tiles of different levels are hidden (skirts or stitching), so no background shows through tile edges at any tilt, and the crack fix never appears as walls or shimmer.
steps: Open `?scenario=terrain-crack-sweep&debug=1`, which forces neighboring tiles of different levels in steep terrain
Record every frame of a scripted tilt and orbit on both backends with the clear color set to a sentinel color
Assert zero sentinel-colored pixels inside the terrain footprint in every frame
Run the temporal glitch detector along tile edges and assert no shimmer, z-fighting or visible vertical walls

features.description: Terrain level changes are geomorphed (or use an equivalent technique), so relief never pops when tiles refine or coarsen.
steps: Open `?scenario=terrain-alps` and record every frame of a slow scripted zoom in and out on both backends
Run the temporal glitch detector (frame differencing) on terrain regions
Assert no frame-to-frame change at a refinement or coarsening event exceeds the popping threshold
Unit test the morph: at the end of each transition the geometry equals the target level's mesh exactly

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: A missing or still-loading terrain tile is covered by its best available ancestor upsampled to the child's area, a parent is never discarded before all replacing children are ready, and areas without terrain coverage render as the no-data surface chosen in the terrain ADR (the ellipsoid or geoid sea level), never as holes and with no step at coverage edges.
steps: Serve fixture terrain with deliberately delayed, missing (404) and out-of-coverage tiles
Navigate the playground over these areas with Playwright on both backends while recording frames with a sentinel clear color
Assert zero sentinel pixels in every frame after the base has loaded
Assert from the tile-state trace that no parent terrain tile is released before all of its replacing children are ready and that 404 tiles are not retried
Assert no step or wall is visible where covered terrain meets uncovered areas, including coastlines at the edge of coverage (seam detector)

features.description: Terrain and imagery choose their levels independently, so detailed imagery is draped on coarser terrain tiles at full sharpness.
steps: Open `?scenario=independent-levels&debug=1` with terrain limited to level 10 and imagery available to level 18
Zoom to street level and read per-tile terrain and imagery levels from the debug overlay data
Assert imagery levels exceed terrain levels and the on-screen imagery texel density matches the imagery-only reference within tolerance
Capture screenshots on both backends and assert no seams where imagery tile edges cross terrain tiles (edge-detection check along tile borders)

features.description: Imagery in one tiling scheme is mapped correctly onto terrain in another (Web Mercator imagery on geographic terrain and vice versa) with no misregistration.
steps: Load a geographic quantized-mesh fixture with Web Mercator imagery containing a georeferenced grid
Assert the grid lines rendered over the terrain land at their expected screen positions within 1 pixel at latitudes 0°, 45° and 75° on both backends
Repeat with Web Mercator heightmap terrain and geographic imagery

features.description: Terrain tile bounding volumes include their minimum and maximum heights, so frustum and horizon culling never remove visible relief such as mountains near the horizon or at the screen edges.
steps: Unit test bounding volumes against fixture tiles: every vertex lies inside its tile's volume
Open `?scenario=terrain-horizon-peaks` with a tall peak just behind the ellipsoid horizon and another at the frustum edge
Record frames while panning on both backends and assert by frame differencing that the peaks never disappear or flicker

features.description: Terrain has no gaps or seams at the antimeridian or near the poles.
steps: Open scenarios with fixture terrain centered on the antimeridian (Fiji) and at high latitudes (Svalbard, the Antarctic coast)
Record frames during a scripted orbit on both backends with a sentinel clear color
Assert zero sentinel pixels and no seam lines (edge-detection along the 180° meridian and the polar cap boundary)

features.description: A synchronous elevation query returns the best-available height at a coordinate from terrain already in memory, together with the level it came from, without allocating.
steps: Unit test the query against fixture tiles at several levels and assert results equal interpolation on the loaded mesh
In the playground, run 10,000 queries per frame at random coordinates and assert the total time stays within its CPU budget with zero heap allocations per query
Assert a query outside terrain coverage returns the height of the no-data surface chosen in the terrain ADR (the ellipsoid or geoid sea level) with a no-data flag

features.description: An asynchronous elevation query loads the most detailed terrain available for a coordinate and resolves with the precise height.
steps: Call the async query over fixture terrain where only coarse tiles are loaded
Assert it loads tiles down to the source's maximum level for that point and resolves with the finest tile's height within the source precision
Issue 1,000 queries over the same area and assert each tile is requested at most once
Assert the promise settles with a typed error (never hangs) when the source fails, times out or the query is cancelled

features.description: The camera never enters the terrain: zooming, panning, rotating and tilting near steep relief keep the camera above the surface by a minimum clearance.
steps: Open `?scenario=terrain-alps` at a valley floor on both backends
Drive 60 s of scripted input toward a cliff: wheel zoom, drag, and tilt and heading changes through the API
In every frame assert the camera height above the terrain at the camera position (finest loaded level) is at least the configured clearance
Assert no frame shows the inside of the terrain (sentinel and back-face checks)

features.description: When finer terrain arrives above the camera's current height, the camera is lifted to the clearance height smoothly and never sits below the displayed surface.
steps: Place the camera just above coarse terrain where the delayed fine tiles are higher
Release the fine tiles and record every frame on both backends
Assert the camera stays above the displayed surface in every frame
Assert the lift spans multiple frames with per-frame displacement below the jump threshold

features.description: Milestone 4 acceptance: no cracks, correct relief, and the camera never enters the terrain.
steps: Run the terrain scenario suite (crack sweep, horizon peaks, Alps zoom, antimeridian, poles, missing tiles) on both backends and assert zero sentinel pixels and no popping
Project 100 known DEM sample points to the screen and assert rendered depth matches their WGS84 positions within tolerance
Run the terrain collision scenario and assert the camera clearance holds in every frame
Run the terrain decoder conformance and fuzz suites and assert they pass
Confirm no known bug remains open for this milestone
A fresh-context reviewer checks the milestone against PLAN.md and its acceptance criteria and reports no correctness or requirement gaps

features.description: In Auto mode the morph factor, tilt and terrain relief are smooth, continuous functions of zoom (easing curves, never thresholds), with tilt starting as the map finishes flattening.
steps: Unit test the curves: sample zoom finely across the full range and assert each curve is continuous, monotonic where specified, and has a bounded derivative
Assert the morph reaches its flat end before tilt exceeds a small epsilon, within the configured overlap

Assert the default phase ranges match the numeric zoom or altitude ranges set in docs/plan for globe (world, continents), flattening (country), 2D map (region, city) and 3D view (neighborhood, street)
Open `?scenario=zoom-globe-to-street` and assert the morph factor, tilt and relief reported per frame follow the curves

features.description: In Auto mode the morph factor, tilt and terrain relief are smooth, continuous functions of zoom (easing curves, never thresholds) that ease in and out at their ends; tilt stays at exactly 0° through the 2D map band (region, city) and rises only at neighborhood scale.
steps: Unit test the curves: sample zoom finely across the full range and assert each curve is continuous, monotonic where specified, has a bounded derivative and a zero derivative at both ends of its transition
Assert tilt is exactly 0° from the globe through the end of the 2D map band and starts rising only at the neighborhood-scale zoom set in docs/plan, after the morph has reached the flat plane

Assert the default phase ranges match the numeric zoom or altitude ranges set in docs/plan for globe (world, continents), flattening (country), 2D map (region, city) and 3D view (neighborhood, street)
Open `?scenario=zoom-globe-to-street` and assert the morph factor, tilt and relief reported per frame follow the curves

features.description: The phase zoom ranges, easing curves, automatic tilt (default within 45–60°) and relief curve are set through typed, validated configuration.
steps: Unit test configuration validation: overlapping or non-monotonic ranges and tilts outside 0–90° are rejected with descriptive errors
Configure custom curves in the playground and assert the reported morph, tilt and relief follow them
Change the curves at runtime and assert the view adapts without a jump (frame differencing)

features.description: At world and continent scale in Auto mode the surface is the WGS84 ellipsoid, the tilt is 0° and the terrain is flat.
steps: Open `?scenario=globe-world` on both backends
Assert through the public camera state: phase globe, applied tilt 0°, relief factor 0
Capture screenshots and assert the diff against the globe baseline is within the visual tolerance
Assert the rendered limb matches the projected WGS84 ellipsoid silhouette within 1 px

features.description: Between the globe and flat phases the surface morphs continuously by interpolating every vertex between its ellipsoid and plane positions on the GPU, with no per-frame CPU re-meshing.
steps: Unit test the morph function shared by the shader and the CPU picking path: factor 0 gives ellipsoid positions, factor 1 gives plane positions, intermediate factors are continuous
Open `?scenario=morph-sweep` and record every frame while the morph factor sweeps 0 → 1 → 0 on both backends
Assert renderer upload counters show no tile geometry re-upload caused by the sweep
Assert frame differencing shows no frame-to-frame jump above the threshold

features.description: At region and city scale the view is a true flat Web Mercator map at 0° tilt with flat or subtle relief.
steps: Open `?scenario=map-2d-city` on both backends
Assert through the public camera state: phase 2D map, morph factor 1, applied tilt 0°, relief factor within the configured 2D range
Capture screenshots and assert they match a reference mosaic of the same Web Mercator tiles within the visual tolerance (parallels and meridians straight and perpendicular)

features.description: At neighborhood and street scale the tilt rises gradually to the configured automatic tilt and terrain relief reaches full height.
steps: Open `?scenario=zoom-city-to-street` on both backends
Zoom continuously with Playwright from city to street scale
Assert the applied tilt increases monotonically to the configured automatic tilt and the relief factor reaches 1
Capture screenshots at fixed zoom levels and assert the diff against the baselines is within the visual tolerance

features.description: During the globe-to-flat morph the geographic point under the cursor stays fixed on screen while zooming with the wheel.
steps: Open `?scenario=morph-anchor` on both backends
Zoom with Playwright wheel events through the whole flattening range with the cursor at the center, the corners and near the limb, and with non-zero heading
In every frame pick the geographic coordinate under the cursor and assert it stays within 1 px of the cursor

features.description: When zoom is not cursor-anchored (API zoom calls), the geographic point at the screen center stays fixed during the morph.
steps: Zoom through the flattening range with the zoom API on both backends
In every frame project the start center coordinate to the screen
Assert it stays within 1 px of the screen center

features.description: On the flat plane terrain heights are scaled by the projection's scale factor, so relief keeps correct proportions at every latitude and changes continuously during the morph.
steps: Unit test the vertical scale: at latitude φ a height h maps to h × k(φ) plane units, where k is the Mercator scale factor
Render the same analytic cone-shaped fixture mountain at latitudes 0°, 45° and 70° in the 3D phase on both backends
Assert its screen-space height-to-base ratio is identical at each latitude within tolerance
Assert the vertical scale interpolates continuously between the ellipsoid and plane values during the morph

features.description: Picked positions and measurements stay on the WGS84 ellipsoid and are identical in the globe, flattening, 2D and 3D phases.
steps: Project known WGS84 coordinates to the screen and pick them back in each phase; assert the round trip is within one pixel's ground distance
Compute the geodesic distance between two picked points with the core geodesic API in each phase and assert identical results
Assert no public measurement or picking API accepts or returns projected plane coordinates

features.description: On the flat map the world wraps horizontally, so panning across the antimeridian is continuous with no gap, seam or jump.
steps: Open `?scenario=map-2d-antimeridian` on both backends
Drag-pan east across 180° several times with Playwright, recording frames with a sentinel clear color
Assert zero sentinel pixels and no seam (edge detection along the wrap line)
Assert the reported center longitude wraps into [−180°, 180°) while the camera motion stays continuous

features.description: Polar regions beyond the Web Mercator limit (about ±85°) stay covered by caps during the morph, in the flat phase and in tilted views, so no gap shows at high latitudes.
steps: Open `?scenario=morph-poles` centered at 80°N and 80°S on both backends
Sweep the morph and the tilt while recording every frame with a sentinel clear color
Assert zero sentinel pixels inside the map area and no seam at the cap boundary

features.description: Auto is the default view mode: on startup and after choosing Auto, the zoom curves drive tilt and relief.
steps: Create an engine without a view-mode option and assert the API reports Auto
Zoom through every phase and assert the applied tilt equals the curve value in every frame
After a manual tilt, select Auto and assert the tilt returns to the curve value without a jump and follows the curves again

features.description: In 2D locked mode the tilt stays at 0° at every zoom while the globe-to-flat morph keeps working, so the user can zoom back out to the globe.
steps: Select 2D locked through the API while in the 3D phase and assert the tilt animates to 0° without a jump
Zoom from street level out to the globe and back in with Playwright
Assert the applied tilt is 0° in every frame and the morph factor follows the zoom curve
