Assert rotation still works and the heading persists

features.description: The 2D / 3D / Auto toggle sets the tilt to 0° (2D), to the configured default tilt (3D) or restores the zoom-driven curves (Auto), and a visible back-to-Auto control sits next to the 2D/3D toggle.
steps: Click the playground 2D, 3D and Auto controls with Playwright and assert the resulting mode, chosen tilt and applied tilt
Assert every change animates without a jump (frame differencing)
Assert the Auto control is visible next to the 2D/3D toggle and reflects the active mode
Repeat through the public API and assert identical results and mode-change events

features.description: The camera stores the user's chosen tilt and heading separately from the applied values, the API exposes both, and no clamp ever overwrites the choice.
steps: Unit test the camera state: clamping changes only applied values
Property test: for random sequences of zoom, pan and constraint changes, the chosen values change only on explicit user or API tilt and heading input
Assert the public camera state exposes chosen and applied tilt and heading and the view mode

features.description: When the chosen tilt would put the camera inside terrain, the applied tilt is clamped temporarily and the chosen tilt is restored smoothly as soon as possible.
steps: Open `?scenario=tilt-clamp-terrain` with a chosen tilt of 70° near a mountain wall on both backends
Move toward and away from the wall with Playwright
Assert the camera never enters the terrain, the applied tilt is reduced only while required and returns to 70° once clear
Assert the chosen tilt stays 70° throughout and every transition is free of jumps

features.description: When the chosen tilt would fill the screen with empty sky at the current altitude, the applied tilt is clamped temporarily and restored when zooming back in.
steps: Choose a 60° tilt at street level, then zoom out to the globe phase
Assert the applied tilt decreases continuously with zoom so the visible empty-sky fraction stays below the configured limit
Zoom back in and assert the applied tilt returns to 60° without a jump
Assert the chosen tilt remains 60° throughout

features.description: Milestone 5 acceptance: a continuous zoom from the globe to an oblique street view is smooth at the target frame rate, with no jumps.
steps: Run `?scenario=zoom-globe-to-street` with fixture imagery and terrain on both backends
Record frame times and assert p95 frame time <= 16.7 ms on the reference desktop
Record frame times on the reference tablet and assert at least 30 fps
Assert per-frame continuity of camera position, tilt, heading, morph factor and relief (no change above the per-frame jump thresholds)
Run the temporal glitch detector and assert no popping, flicker or seams; repeat in 2D-locked and manual-tilt modes
Confirm no known bug remains open for this milestone
A fresh-context reviewer checks the milestone against PLAN.md and its acceptance criteria and reports no correctness or requirement gaps

features.description: Mouse-wheel zoom is smooth, time-based and anchored at the cursor: the geographic point under the cursor (on terrain in tilted views) stays under it.
steps: Open the playground on both backends at globe, 2D and tilted 3D views with terrain
Dispatch wheel events in line and pixel delta modes at several cursor positions with Playwright
In every frame pick the coordinate under the cursor and assert it stays within 1 px of the cursor
Assert each notch animates over several frames with eased velocity, and that a wheel event over empty sky zooms toward the screen center

features.description: Trackpad scrolling and trackpad pinch (wheel events with ctrlKey and small pixel deltas) zoom smoothly and continuously at the cursor, distinct from mouse-wheel notches.
steps: Replay recorded macOS and Windows trackpad wheel sequences (pixel deltas and ctrlKey pinch) with Playwright
Assert the zoom changes in proportion to the deltas with no stepping (no frame-to-frame jump above threshold) and stays anchored within 1 px
Manually check on a macOS trackpad and a Windows precision touchpad and record the result

features.description: Double-click zooms in by one level, animated and anchored at the clicked point.
steps: Double-click at several positions with Playwright on both backends
Assert the zoom increases by exactly one level at the end of the animation and the clicked coordinate stays within 1 px of the pointer
Assert a single click does not zoom

features.description: Double-tap zooms in by one level, animated and anchored at the tapped point.
steps: Dispatch double taps under Playwright touch emulation at several positions
Assert the zoom increases by exactly one level and the tapped coordinate stays within 1 px of the tap point
Assert a single tap and a tap followed by a drag do not trigger it
Manually check on the reference tablet

features.description: A two-finger tap zooms out by one level around the midpoint of the two touches.
steps: Dispatch a two-finger tap under touch emulation
Assert the zoom decreases by exactly one level around the touch midpoint
Assert two-finger touches that move beyond the tap tolerance or last beyond the tap duration do not trigger it
Manually check on the reference tablet

features.description: Pinch zoom on touch screens is continuous and anchored at the midpoint between the fingers.
steps: Dispatch pinch gestures under touch emulation in globe, 2D and 3D views on both backends
In every frame assert the coordinate under the touch midpoint stays within 1 px of it
Assert the zoom tracks the finger distance continuously and ends with eased inertia
Manually check on the reference tablet
Pinch through the globe-to-flat morph range and assert the geographic point under the finger midpoint stays within 1 px of it in every frame

features.description: Zoom-in and zoom-out commands (the +/- buttons and API) zoom smoothly by one level around the screen center, and rapid presses accumulate without stutter.
steps: Click the playground +/- buttons and call the zoom-in and zoom-out API
Assert ±1 level per press with the center coordinate fixed
Press five times rapidly and assert the target accumulates to five levels with continuous motion (no frame-to-frame jump)
Zoom through the globe-to-flat morph range with the buttons and the keyboard and assert the geographic point at the screen center stays within 1 px of it in every frame

features.description: Shift+drag draws a zoom box, releasing it fits the boxed area to the view, and Escape cancels it.
steps: Shift+drag a rectangle with Playwright and assert the box overlay is drawn during the drag
On release assert the box's geographic corners are inside the viewport and the view fills the box's larger dimension within tolerance
Press Escape during a box drag and assert nothing moves

features.description: Fitting to geographic bounds, including bounds that cross the antimeridian or reach high latitudes, shows the whole area inside the viewport minus the requested padding, with any heading and tilt.
steps: Call fit-to-bounds for a city, a country, a Pacific area crossing the antimeridian and a near-polar area, with several paddings, headings and tilts
After the animation, project the bounds' corners and edge samples to the screen
Assert all are inside the padded viewport and at least one edge touches the padding within 2 px

features.description: Zoom is continuous and fractional: the API accepts and reports fractional zoom, and the view never snaps to integer levels.
steps: Set zoom 10.37 through the API and assert the reported zoom is 10.37
Zoom continuously with a trackpad sequence and assert the reported zoom changes without quantization
Assert the ground distance per pixel at the center changes continuously across integer zoom boundaries

features.description: Dragging pans the map so the grabbed geographic point stays under the pointer in globe, flat and tilted views, including near the poles and across the antimeridian, without flips.
steps: Drag with Playwright in globe, 2D and tilted 3D views on both backends, including drags across the antimeridian and near 89°N
In every frame assert the grabbed coordinate stays within 1 px of the pointer while it is on the surface
Assert the globe never flips or jumps when the drag passes near a pole
Under touch emulation drag with one finger and assert the same behavior

features.description: Releasing a drag with velocity continues the motion with time-based inertia that decelerates smoothly to rest, while a release after holding still does not coast.
steps: Drag and release at speed with Playwright and record the camera per frame
Assert the velocity at release matches the drag velocity, then decays monotonically to zero within the configured time
Assert a release after the pointer was held still produces no inertia
Assert inertia on the globe continues along the drag's great-circle direction
Repeat with a one-finger touch drag and release and assert the same inertia behavior

features.description: A two-finger drag pans the map on touch screens, keeping the content under the fingers' midpoint.
steps: Dispatch two-finger parallel drags under touch emulation on both backends
Assert the coordinate under the touch midpoint follows the midpoint within 1 px
Assert release with velocity produces the same inertia as a mouse drag
Manually check on the reference tablet

features.description: Arrow keys pan the view smoothly while held, with an eased start and stop, when the map has keyboard focus.
steps: Focus the map and hold each arrow key with Playwright
Assert the view pans in the matching screen direction with eased acceleration and deceleration and no stutter
Assert the keys do nothing when focus is outside the map

features.description: Right-drag rotates the heading (horizontal motion) and tilts the view (vertical motion) around the screen-center target without opening the context menu.
steps: Right-drag horizontally and vertically with Playwright on both backends
Assert the heading changes with horizontal motion, the tilt with vertical motion, and the center target stays fixed
Assert no context menu appears and the new tilt and heading become the chosen values

features.description: Ctrl+drag with the primary button rotates and tilts exactly like right-drag.
steps: Ctrl+drag horizontally and vertically with Playwright
Assert the heading and tilt change exactly as for an equivalent right-drag
Assert releasing Ctrl mid-drag ends the rotation without a jump

features.description: Twisting two fingers rotates the heading around the touch midpoint, combined smoothly with pinch and pan in the same gesture.
steps: Dispatch two-finger twist gestures, alone and combined with pinch and pan, under touch emulation
Assert the heading follows the twist angle and the coordinate under the midpoint stays under it
Assert small unintended twists during a pinch below the rotation threshold do not rotate
Manually check on the reference tablet

features.description: A two-finger vertical drag tilts the view on touch screens and is not confused with pinch, pan or rotate.
steps: Dispatch two-finger parallel vertical drags under touch emulation
Assert the tilt changes with the vertical motion and becomes the chosen tilt
Assert pinch, twist and two-finger pan gestures do not trigger tilt
Manually check on the reference tablet

features.description: Adding or lifting fingers mid-gesture (one to two fingers and back) continues the gesture without a jump.
steps: Under touch emulation, start a one-finger pan, add a second finger, pinch, lift one finger and keep panning
Record the camera per frame and assert no frame-to-frame change above the jump threshold at each finger change
Manually check on the reference tablet

features.description: Shift+Left/Right rotate and Shift+Up/Down tilt the view smoothly while held.
steps: Focus the map and hold Shift with each arrow key in Playwright
Assert the heading changes with Left/Right and the tilt with Up/Down, eased, with no stutter
Assert the resulting tilt and heading become the chosen values

features.description: A tilt control (API and playground control) sets the tilt with a smooth animation, respecting the view-mode rules and the maximum tilt.
steps: Use the playground tilt control and the tilt API to set several tilts
Assert the tilt animates to the value, becomes the chosen tilt and never exceeds the maximum tilt
Assert using it in 2D locked or Auto mode follows the documented view-mode rules

features.description: Navigation input over the map never scrolls or zooms the host page, while page scrolling outside the map is unaffected.
steps: Embed the engine in a scrollable test page
Wheel, pinch and touch-drag over the map and assert the window scroll position and visual viewport scale do not change
Wheel outside the map and assert the page scrolls normally

features.description: Compass behavior: the compass shows the applied heading every frame, a click rotates the view to north up, and dragging the compass rotates the view.
steps: Rotate the view and assert the playground compass angle equals the applied heading in every frame
Click the compass and assert the heading animates to 0° while center and tilt are kept
Drag around the compass and assert the heading follows the drag angle
Repeat the click and drag under touch emulation

features.description: One-click orientation commands rotate the view to face north, east, south or west.
steps: Trigger each orientation command from the playground and the API
Assert the heading animates to 0°, 90°, 180° and 270° respectively along the shortest arc
Assert the center and tilt are kept and the new heading becomes the chosen heading

features.description: The camera orbits around a picked or given geographic point, keeping it fixed on screen, interactively and as a cancellable continuous animation.
steps: Start an orbit around a picked point and around a point given through the API on both backends
In every frame assert the orbit point stays within 1 px of its screen position and the camera distance to it is constant
Assert user input or a cancel call stops the orbit without a jump

features.description: Reset to the globe animates out to a full-globe view centered on the current location.
steps: Trigger reset to the globe from street level through the playground and the API
Assert the animation ends with the whole globe visible and centered on the previous center longitude and latitude
Assert the movement events and promise report completion

features.description: A project home view can be configured, and the home command flies to it.
steps: Configure a home view (center, zoom, heading, tilt, view mode) and trigger the home command from the playground and the API
Assert the camera arrives exactly at the home view
Assert an invalid home view is rejected by configuration validation

features.description: flyTo animates along a curved zoom-out/zoom-in path (van Wijk and Nuij), with automatic or specified duration, and ends exactly at the target.
steps: Call flyTo between distant and between nearby targets
Record the camera per frame and assert the zoom profile rises then falls as the van Wijk–Nuij path predicts, with near-constant perceived screen velocity
Assert the final camera state equals the target within floating-point tolerance
Assert duration, speed, curve and easing options are honored and invalid values are rejected

features.description: Long flights pass through the phases on their own: a flight from Milan to Tokyo rises into the globe phase and descends back to the tilted 3D view.
steps: From a tilted street view in Milan in Auto mode, call flyTo to a street view in Tokyo on both backends
Record the camera state per frame and assert the phase sequence 3D → 2D → flattening → globe → flattening → 2D → 3D
Assert continuity of morph factor, tilt and relief in every frame (no jump)
Record frames and assert zero black or empty pixels after the base has loaded

features.description: jumpTo teleports the camera to the target in a single frame with no animation and emits the movement events.
steps: Call jumpTo with several targets
Assert the next rendered frame shows the target camera state exactly
Assert movestart, move and moveend fire once each and the promise or return value reports completion

features.description: easeTo performs short moves with eased interpolation of center, zoom, heading and tilt, taking the shortest heading arc and the short way across the antimeridian.
steps: Call easeTo for short moves changing each camera parameter
Assert the eased interpolation per frame and the exact final state
Assert heading 350° → 10° passes through 0° and a move from 179°E to 179°W crosses the antimeridian

features.description: Tours play a queue of waypoints in order, each with its own movement type, duration and dwell time, and are cancellable.
steps: Start a tour of five waypoints mixing flyTo and easeTo legs with dwell times
Assert the camera reaches each waypoint in order and emits a waypoint event for each
Assert the tour promise settles as completed at the end, and as interrupted when cancelled or when the user takes over mid-tour

features.description: Every movement call returns a promise that settles when the movement completes or is interrupted (reporting which, never hanging), and emits movestart, move and moveend events with their cause.
steps: Call flyTo, easeTo, jumpTo and a tour and assert each promise settles as completed
Start a second movement during the first and assert the first settles as interrupted
Cancel flyTo, easeTo and a tour through their cancel() method and through an AbortSignal, and assert each promise settles as cancelled and the camera stays where it stopped
Assert events fire in order with their cause (user, API, inertia) and that move fires at most once per frame
Assert calls with invalid arguments reject with typed validation errors without moving the camera

features.description: flyTo, easeTo, jumpTo and tours keep the user's chosen tilt, heading and view mode unless the call specifies them, and a manual tilt persists through flights.
steps: Set a manual tilt of 40° and heading 70°, then call each movement API without tilt or heading
Assert the chosen tilt and heading are kept on arrival, including after flights that pass through the globe phase
Call each movement API with an explicit tilt and heading and assert they are applied
Assert the view mode is unchanged by every movement call

features.description: Any user input (wheel, drag, touch, keyboard) interrupts a running animation or inertia and takes over smoothly from the current state without a jump.
steps: Start flyTo, easeTo, a tour, an orbit and drag inertia, and interrupt each with wheel, drag, touch and keyboard input in Playwright
Record the camera per frame and assert no frame-to-frame change above the jump threshold at the takeover
Assert the interrupted movement's promise settles as interrupted

features.description: All animations and inertia are frame-rate independent: the camera follows the same trajectory at 30, 60, 120 and 144 Hz and after stalled frames.
steps: Run the same flyTo, easeTo, inertia and keyboard-pan sequences with a controlled clock at 30, 60, 120 and 144 Hz
Assert the camera states at equal timestamps match within tolerance
Inject a 250 ms stall mid-animation and assert the camera continues from the time-correct position without overshoot

features.description: Go to coordinates accepts decimal degrees in common notations (signed, with N/S/E/W prefixes or suffixes, comma- or space-separated) and flies there.
steps: Unit test the parser on a table of notations, e.g. `45.4642, 9.19`, `45.4642N 9.19E`, `N45.4642 E9.19`, `-33.86 151.21`
Assert hemisphere letters decide the axes when present and the documented latitude, longitude order applies otherwise
Type a coordinate into the playground go-to input with Playwright and assert the camera flies to it

features.description: Go to coordinates accepts degrees-minutes-seconds and degrees-decimal-minutes, with typographic (° ′ ″) or ASCII (' ") symbols.
steps: Unit test the parser on a table including `45°27'51.1"N 9°11'24.0"E`, `45° 27.852′ N, 9° 11.4′ E` and their negative and southern/western variants
Assert parsed values equal the expected decimal degrees within 1e-9°
Type a DMS coordinate into the playground go-to input and assert the camera flies to it

features.description: Go to coordinates accepts WGS84 UTM coordinates with zone and latitude band or hemisphere (for example `32T 514000 5034000`), including the Norway and Svalbard zone exceptions.
steps: Unit test UTM conversion against reference points in zones 32 and 33 over Italy and in both hemispheres within 1 mm
Assert the Norway and Svalbard zone exceptions and band letters are validated
Type a UTM coordinate into the playground go-to input and assert the camera flies to it

features.description: The coordinate parsers and formatters round-trip and are fuzzed: format then parse returns the same position within the format's precision, and malformed input returns a typed error without moving the camera.
steps: Run property-based tests over random positions, including the poles, the antimeridian and UTM zone edges, for DD, DMS and UTM round trips
Run the coordinate-string fuzzer for its iteration budget and assert no exception escapes and no input hangs
Assert invalid inputs (latitude above 90°, zone 61, mixed garbage) return typed errors and the go-to input shows the error without moving the camera

features.description: A pluggable geocoder interface lets applications supply their own search provider; no provider is bundled and no geocoding request is made by default.
steps: Register a mock geocoder through the public interface and search from the playground
Assert results are returned with positions and bounds and choosing one flies there
Assert that without a registered geocoder no network request is made and the search reports that no provider is configured
Assert no geocoding provider is a dependency of any package

features.description: Minimum and maximum zoom constraints hold for every input and animation, and reaching them eases to a stop without bouncing or jumping.
steps: Configure min and max zoom and drive wheel, pinch, double-click, keyboard, buttons, flyTo and easeTo beyond them
Assert the zoom never leaves the range in any frame
Assert the approach to the limit decelerates smoothly with no frame-to-frame jump

features.description: A maximum tilt constraint caps the tilt for every input, view mode and animation.
steps: Configure a maximum tilt and drive right-drag, two-finger tilt, Shift+arrows, the tilt control, view modes and movement API calls beyond it
Assert the applied and chosen tilt never exceed the maximum in any frame
Assert the approach to the limit is smooth

features.description: Optional geographic bounds keep the view inside a configured area (including bounds crossing the antimeridian) for panning, zooming and flights, easing against the edges.
steps: Configure bounds and drive drag, inertia, keyboard pan, wheel zoom-out and flyTo targets outside them
Assert the view center stays inside the bounds in every frame and edge contact decelerates smoothly
Repeat with bounds crossing the antimeridian and assert correct behavior on both sides

features.description: flyTo, easeTo, orbit and tour paths never pass through terrain: the camera is kept above the relief along the way.
steps: Fly and ease between points on opposite sides of a fixture mountain range at low altitude, and orbit at low altitude around a summit
In every frame assert the camera clearance above the terrain is at least the configured minimum
Assert the path adjustment is continuous (no jump) and the arrival state equals the target

features.description: Every navigation action is operable with the keyboard alone, with visible focus on the map and a documented key map that does not capture keys typed into page inputs.
steps: Tab to the map with Playwright and assert a visible focus indicator
Perform zoom in and out, pan, rotate, tilt, reset north, home and view-mode changes using only keyboard events
Assert the key map is documented and that keys typed into a text input elsewhere on the page do not move the map

features.description: With the system reduced-motion setting, flights become quick fades and inertia and other large animated movements are minimized, following setting changes at runtime.
steps: Emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce with Playwright
Call flyTo and assert the view cross-fades to the destination within the configured short duration without traversing the path
Assert drag inertia is disabled or shortened as documented
Toggle the setting at runtime and assert behavior follows without a reload

features.description: When the user tilts by hand, that tilt becomes the chosen tilt and persists at every zoom, including the globe phase, until the user tilts again or picks another view mode.
steps: In Auto mode tilt to 30° with a right-drag and assert the API reports manual mode with chosen tilt 30°
Zoom out to the globe phase and back to street level; assert the chosen tilt stays 30° and the applied tilt equals 30° wherever it is not clamped
Tilt again to 50° and assert the chosen tilt becomes 50°
Select 2D, 3D and Auto in turn and assert each replaces the manual tilt as specified

features.description: The chosen heading persists at every zoom, phase and view mode until the user changes it; there is no automatic north-up.
steps: Rotate to heading 120° with a right-drag and, under touch emulation, with a two-finger rotate
Zoom out to the globe and back, switch view modes, and assert the heading stays 120°
Assert only an explicit user action (compass, orientation commands) or an API call that specifies a heading changes it

features.description: Milestone 6 acceptance: every listed interaction works on desktop and tablet.
steps: Run the full navigation Playwright suite (mouse, keyboard and touch emulation) on both backends
Run the manual tablet checklist on the reference tablets (iPadOS Safari, Android Chrome) and record the results in the repository
Assert frame-rate targets during interaction: p95 frame time <= 16.7 ms on the reference desktop and at least 30 fps on the reference tablet
Confirm no known bug remains open for this milestone
A fresh-context reviewer checks the milestone against PLAN.md and its acceptance criteria and reports no correctness or requirement gaps

features.description: A written research survey on source adapters, tile formats and reprojection exists in docs/research/, covering how the studied engines model sources, tiling schemes, coverage, attribution and provider terms, their known failure modes, and the chosen approach with its reasons.
steps: Open the source-adapters survey in docs/research/ and confirm it covers CesiumJS, OpenLayers, MapLibre GL JS, Leaflet, iTowns, OpenGlobus and loaders.gl, plus the PMTiles, MBTiles, WMTS, WMS, quantized-mesh and Mapbox Vector Tile specifications
Confirm it records the approaches found for tiling schemes, custom tile matrix sets, raster reprojection, source fallback, color matching and attribution, with their trade-offs

Confirm it lists known bugs and complaints from those projects' issue trackers (for example seams after reprojection, WMS axis-order mistakes, missing attribution) and how the chosen design avoids each
Confirm it lists how those projects test their adapters (fixtures, live endpoints, conformance suites)
Confirm it states the chosen approach and why, links the ADRs that record the decisions, and states that no code was copied and only open-source projects were studied

features.description: A consumer can write their own adapter for each source kind (imagery, terrain, vector, 3D) against the common plugin interface, outside the engine packages, and attach it without changing engine code.
steps: Create a test package outside packages/ that depends only on the public engine API and implements one custom adapter per kind (imagery, terrain, vector, 3D) for an unusual fixture service
Type-check the test package in strict mode with no `any`
Attach the custom imagery and terrain adapters in the playground through the public API and capture screenshots on WebGPU and forced WebGL2 (?backend=webgl2)

Assert the custom imagery and terrain render with zero black pixels after the base has loaded, and the custom vector and 3D adapters deliver their parsed content through the public API at the expected coordinates
Run the shared runtime contract test against every built-in adapter and every custom adapter and assert all pass

features.description: Every source declares its metadata (tiling scheme and reference system, coverage bounds, zoom range, tile size, attribution, cache and offline permissions, authentication headers or tokens, rate limits), and the engine validates it when the source is added.
steps: Add fixture sources with complete metadata through the public API and read the metadata back through the source inspection API and the debug overlay (?debug=1)
In a Vitest suite, add sources with missing, malformed or contradictory metadata (unknown reference system, inverted bounds, minimum zoom above maximum zoom, zero tile size, negative rate limit)
Assert each invalid source is rejected with a typed, descriptive error while the engine keeps rendering the other layers
Fuzz source configuration objects and assert no input crashes the engine or blanks the view

features.description: Outside a source's declared zoom range the engine never requests tiles: beyond the maximum zoom it upsamples the deepest available level, and below the minimum zoom the layers underneath show through, with no black areas.
steps: Configure a fixture imagery source limited to zoom 3 to 12 above a base layer in the playground
Run a scripted zoom from the globe to street level with Playwright request interception and record every frame
Assert no request is made for levels outside 3 to 12
Assert that above zoom 12 the view shows upsampled level-12 imagery, that below zoom 3 the base layer shows through, and that every frame has zero black pixels
Repeat on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: A rate limit declared in a source's metadata is enforced by the request scheduler, so the source never receives more requests per second than declared, even during fast flights.
steps: Configure a fixture source with a declared limit of 10 requests per second next to an unlimited fixture source
Run a fast pan and a long flight scenario with Playwright and log request timestamps per host
Assert no one-second window exceeds 10 requests to the limited source while the other source is not slowed down
Assert the view keeps showing parent-tile fallback with zero black pixels while requests are throttled

features.description: Every adapter runs a shared conformance test suite against recorded fixtures in CI and, where the provider's terms allow it, against the provider's real public endpoints in an opt-in job.
steps: Run `npm test` and confirm the conformance suite runs for every built-in adapter against fixtures
Assert the suite checks metadata, tile addressing, coverage, zoom range, error handling (404, 500, timeouts, corrupted payloads), cancellation, attribution and provider-profile enforcement
Run the opt-in live-endpoint job and confirm it targets only endpoints whose terms allow automated testing, and that it records which endpoints were skipped and why
Import the suite from a custom adapter package and assert it runs there unchanged

features.description: Web Mercator (EPSG:3857) tile pyramids render with every tile at its exact geographic bounds on the globe, the flat map and the tilted view, up to about ±85.05° latitude.
steps: Load a fixture Web Mercator pyramid whose tiles show their z/x/y and grid lines at known coordinates
Capture screenshots at globe, 2D and 3D zooms on WebGPU and forced WebGL2 and compare with baselines within the visual-test tolerance
Assert grid lines land within half a pixel of their projected positions
Unit-test tile-to-bounds and bounds-to-tile conversions with property-based round trips

features.description: Geographic (plate carrée, EPSG:4326) tile pyramids, including the two-root-tile layout, render on the globe and the flat map with correct placement and no seam at the antimeridian or the poles.
steps: Load a fixture EPSG:4326 pyramid with two root tiles and labeled grid lines
Capture screenshots at globe and 2D zooms, around the antimeridian and over both poles, on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Assert grid lines are within half a pixel of their expected positions and zero black pixels appear at the antimeridian and the poles
Stack it above a Web Mercator layer and assert both align at test markers

features.description: Raster sources in another reference system, such as Italian data in UTM zones 32N and 33N (EPSG:32632, EPSG:32633), are reprojected and line up with Web Mercator sources in the globe, 2D and 3D phases.
steps: Serve fixture raster tiles in EPSG:32632 and EPSG:32633 that cover the zone boundary at 12°E and contain ground control markers at known WGS84 coordinates
Show them over a Web Mercator reference layer in the playground and capture screenshots in the globe, 2D and 3D phases on both backends
Assert the ground control markers align with the reference layer within half a pixel at native resolution
Record frames while panning across the 12°E boundary and assert no gap, seam or overlap appears between the two zones
Unit-test the reprojection against a projection library reference with property-based round trips

features.description: When a service can deliver a supported reference system (a WMS CRS or a WMTS tile matrix set in EPSG:3857 or EPSG:4326), the adapter requests it directly instead of reprojecting on the client.
steps: Point the WMS and WMTS adapters at fixture capabilities documents that offer both EPSG:32632 and EPSG:3857
Assert through request interception that the adapter requests EPSG:3857 and performs no client-side reprojection
Point them at fixture services that offer only EPSG:32632 and assert the adapter reprojects on the client with correct alignment
Set a preferred reference system in the source configuration and assert it is honored

features.description: Custom TMS and WMTS tile matrix sets in any reference system (non-standard origins, non-power-of-two scale ratios, different matrix sizes per level, non-256 tile sizes) render correctly through reprojection.
steps: Serve fixture WMTS capabilities with a custom tile matrix set in EPSG:25832 (top-left origin, non-power-of-two scale denominators, partial matrices per level, 512-pixel tiles)
Show it over a Web Mercator reference in the playground and capture screenshots at several zooms on both backends
Assert ground control markers align within half a pixel and no seam appears between neighboring tiles or levels
Unit-test that the level chosen for a view follows the screen-space-error rule with the custom resolutions

features.description: The XYZ/TMS tile URL adapter supports URL templates ({z}, {x}, {y}, subdomains, @2x variants), TMS y-flipped addressing and custom request headers, and passes its conformance suite.
steps: Run the XYZ/TMS conformance suite against fixture servers using XYZ and TMS addressing
Assert requested URLs match the template for every tested tile, subdomains rotate deterministically, and TMS rows are flipped
Show both fixtures in the playground and assert tiles land at the correct positions within half a pixel on both backends
Fuzz URL templates and assert invalid templates are rejected with a descriptive error

features.description: The WMTS adapter reads GetCapabilities documents, supports KVP and RESTful encodings, every tile matrix set, style and dimension parameter they declare, and passes its conformance suite.
steps: Run the WMTS conformance suite against fixture capabilities documents from several real-world servers (recorded) and synthetic edge cases
Assert layers, styles, formats, tile matrix sets, tile matrix limits and dimensions are parsed correctly
Assert KVP and RESTful requests are built correctly and tiles land at the correct positions in the playground on both backends
Fuzz capabilities documents and assert malformed input produces a descriptive error and never crashes the engine

features.description: The WMS adapter requests one GetMap image per tile in WMS 1.1.1 and 1.3.0 (including the 1.3.0 latitude-first axis order for EPSG:4326), supports transparent layers and uses a gutter so labels are not cut at tile edges, and passes its conformance suite.
steps: Run the WMS conformance suite against a fixture WMS server in versions 1.1.1 and 1.3.0
Assert BBOX axis order, CRS/SRS parameter, size, format and transparency are correct for each version
Show a fixture layer with labels crossing tile edges in the playground and assert no label is cut and no seam is visible at tile edges on both backends
Fuzz GetCapabilities and service exception responses and assert they never crash the engine

features.description: The PMTiles adapter reads raster tiles from a PMTiles archive over HTTP range requests and from a local file, caching the header and directories, and passes its conformance suite.
steps: Run the PMTiles conformance suite against fixture archives (version 3, clustered and unclustered, with leaf directories and compressed directories)
Assert tiles are fetched with range requests, the header and directories are fetched once per archive, and missing tiles are reported as no data
Load the same archive from a local file (File or Blob) and assert identical tiles
Fuzz archive headers and directories and assert corrupted archives never crash the engine or blank the view

features.description: The MBTiles adapter reads raster tiles from an MBTiles (SQLite) package from a local file or a LAN server, and passes its conformance suite.
steps: Run the MBTiles conformance suite against fixture packages with TMS row order, metadata table and both the plain and the deduplicated (map/images) schema
Assert metadata (bounds, zoom range, format, attribution) is read and tiles are returned for the correct z/x/y
Load the same package from a local file and from a fixture HTTP server and assert identical tiles in the playground
Fuzz package files and assert corrupted databases produce a descriptive error and never crash the engine

features.description: A single georeferenced image (a PNG, JPEG or WebP with explicit bounds or a world file, or a GeoTIFF) is shown at its exact location, reprojected when needed and split for GPU texture limits, and passes its conformance suite.
steps: Run the single-image conformance suite with fixture images georeferenced by bounds, by world file and by GeoTIFF tags, in EPSG:4326, EPSG:3857 and EPSG:32632
Show each in the playground over a reference layer and assert ground control markers align within half a pixel on both backends
Load an image larger than the device's maximum texture size and assert it displays completely with no seams
Fuzz the world-file and GeoTIFF parsers and assert malformed files never crash the engine

features.description: The terrain adapters (quantized-mesh, Terrarium and Terrain-RGB heightmaps) pass the shared adapter conformance suite.
steps: Run the shared conformance suite against the quantized-mesh, Terrarium and Terrain-RGB adapters with fixture tiles
Assert metadata, tile addressing, coverage, zoom range, error handling, cancellation and attribution checks pass for each
Assert heights decoded at test coordinates match the fixture reference values within the encoding's precision

features.description: The GeoJSON adapter parses every geometry type (Point, MultiPoint, LineString, MultiLineString, Polygon with holes, MultiPolygon, GeometryCollection), feature ids and properties in a worker, and passes its conformance suite.
steps: Run the GeoJSON conformance suite against fixtures covering every geometry type, nested collections, antimeridian-crossing geometries and large files (100 MB)
Assert parsed features match the expected engine data structures, coordinates are interpreted as WGS84 longitude-latitude, and parsing happens off the main thread
Assert invalid documents (wrong nesting, NaN coordinates, unclosed rings) are reported per feature without dropping valid features
Fuzz the parser and assert no input crashes the engine

features.description: The KML adapter parses KML documents and KMZ archives (placemarks, points, lines, polygons, MultiGeometry, folders, styles and StyleMaps, ExtendedData, altitude modes, ground overlays), and passes its conformance suite.
steps: Run the KML conformance suite against fixtures exported from common GIS tools and synthetic edge cases
Assert geometries, styles, folder structure, extended data and altitude modes map to the expected engine data structures
Assert a KMZ archive with embedded icons and a ground overlay image parses into the expected engine data structures, with the icons and the overlay image extracted with their placement
Fuzz KML and KMZ input and assert no input crashes the engine

features.description: The GPX adapter parses waypoints, routes and tracks with segments, elevation and time, and passes its conformance suite.
steps: Run the GPX conformance suite against fixtures from common GPS devices and apps (GPX 1.0 and 1.1)
Assert waypoints, routes, track segments, elevations and timestamps map to the expected engine data structures
Fuzz GPX input and assert no input crashes the engine

features.description: The Mapbox Vector Tile (MVT) adapter decodes layers, features, geometry commands, extents and property values in a worker, and passes its conformance suite.
steps: Run the MVT conformance suite against the official vector-tile specification fixtures and real-world tiles (recorded)
Assert decoded layers, feature ids, geometry types, coordinates (extent-scaled) and typed property values match the expected output
Assert decoding happens off the main thread
Fuzz tile payloads and assert malformed tiles are treated as no data and never crash the engine

features.description: Sources with 256-pixel and 512-pixel tiles show the same sharpness at the same zoom, because level selection accounts for tile size.
steps: Serve the same fixture imagery as a 256-pixel pyramid and as a 512-pixel pyramid
Show each in the playground at the same camera views on both backends and capture screenshots
Assert the pixel difference between the two is within the visual-test tolerance and on-screen texel density matches within 10%
Assert the 512-pixel source requests about one quarter as many tiles for the same view

features.description: High-DPI (@2x) tile variants are used on screens with a device pixel ratio above 1 and are drawn at the correct geographic size.
steps: Configure a fixture source with 1x and @2x URL templates
Open the playground with Playwright at deviceScaleFactor 1 and 2 and intercept requests
Assert @2x tiles are requested only at device pixel ratio 2 and that fixture labels appear at the same CSS size in both screenshots
Assert changing the resolution scale setting changes which variant is requested

features.description: Tiles in every image format the browser decodes (PNG with and without alpha, JPEG, WebP, AVIF) render identically, and a format the current browser cannot decode is treated as no data instead of breaking the view.
steps: Serve the same fixture pyramid as PNG, JPEG, WebP and AVIF
Render each in the playground on both backends and compare screenshots with the PNG reference within each format's tolerance
Assert transparent PNG and WebP areas show the layer below
Force AVIF decoding to fail and assert those tiles fall back to the parent or the layer below with zero black pixels and a logged warning

features.description: Layers stack in a defined order that the app can change at runtime, and the new order shows on the next frame without flicker.
steps: Add three overlapping fixture imagery layers with distinct colors in the playground
Reorder them through the public API while recording frames
Assert the top layer's color is visible in the overlap after each change and no frame shows a missing layer or black pixels
Repeat on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: Each layer has an opacity from 0 to 1, changeable at runtime and applied correctly over the layers below.
steps: Set a fixture layer's opacity to 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 through the public API
Capture screenshots and assert sampled pixel colors match the expected blend within tolerance on both backends
Animate opacity over 1 s while recording frames and assert the change is monotonic with no flicker
Assert a layer at opacity 0 issues no new tile requests

features.description: Each layer can be shown or hidden at runtime; a hidden layer stops requesting tiles, and showing it again reuses cached tiles without blank frames.
steps: Hide and show a fixture layer through the public API while recording frames and requests
Assert a hidden layer makes no new requests and is not drawn
Assert showing it again draws its cached tiles on the next frame and no frame shows black pixels
Repeat on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: Layers support blending modes (at least normal, multiply and screen), so overlays such as hillshade combine correctly with imagery.
steps: Stack a fixture hillshade over fixture imagery with normal, multiply and screen blending
Capture screenshots and compare with reference images computed from the blend formulas within tolerance
Assert WebGPU and forced WebGL2 results match within the visual-test tolerance

features.description: A layer can have a chain of sources with priorities (for example an offline base first and online detail second), and each tile comes automatically from the highest-priority source whose coverage includes it.
steps: Configure a layer whose chain is a fixture package covering the world to zoom 8 and an online fixture source covering Italy to zoom 18
Run a scripted zoom into Rome and a pan from Rome to Paris with request interception
Assert tiles inside Italy above zoom 8 come from the online source, tiles outside its coverage are never requested from it, and the package supplies everything else
Record frames and assert zero black pixels and no visible seam at the coverage boundary

features.description: When a source in a chain is unavailable (errors, timeouts, offline), the layer falls back automatically to the next available source and switches back when the source recovers, without black areas.
steps: Configure a layer with two fixture sources of the same area
During a pan scenario, make the first source return 500 errors, then time out, then recover, using Playwright route interception
Assert tiles come from the second source while the first is failing and return to the first after recovery
Record frames and assert zero black pixels and no popping during each switch

features.description: When a layer switches between sources with different tones, the engine blends or adjusts colors so neither the switch nor the boundary between sources is visible.
steps: Configure a chain whose two fixture sources image the same area with clearly different brightness and color balance
Record frames while zooming and panning across the coverage boundary on both backends
Assert the mean color difference across the boundary stays below the visual-test threshold
Assert frame-difference analysis shows no visible jump when the active source switches
Disable harmonization for the layer and assert the raw source colors are shown

features.description: A source looks and behaves the same in the globe, 2D and 3D phases: same colors, same placement, same attribution and the same loading behavior.
steps: Show a fixture source with ground control markers in the playground
Capture screenshots of the same area at the end of the globe phase, in the 2D phase and in the 3D phase on both backends
Assert markers align within half a pixel in every phase and mean colors differ by less than the visual-test tolerance
Assert attribution and request patterns are the same in every phase

features.description: Fetching is CORS-aware: cross-origin tiles with correct CORS headers are used as textures, a source without CORS produces a clear diagnostic instead of a tainted or crashed renderer, and the credentials mode is configurable per source.
steps: Serve fixture tiles from a second origin with and without Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers
Assert tiles with CORS headers render on both backends
Assert a source without CORS logs one descriptive error naming the source, its tiles are treated as unavailable, and the rest of the view keeps rendering with zero black pixels
Set the credentials mode per source and assert requests are sent with the configured mode

features.description: Each source can have its own authentication headers or tokens, sent only to that source's hosts, with a callback to refresh expiring tokens.
steps: Configure two fixture sources with different authorization headers and a token-refresh callback on one of them
Assert through request interception that each header reaches only its own source's hosts
Make the fixture server reject an expired token and assert the callback is called, the request is retried with the new token, and no black pixels appear
Assert tokens never appear in logs, traces, the debug overlay or error messages

features.description: Secrets stay out of URLs: credentials are sent in headers wherever the provider supports it, and where a provider requires a key in the URL, that key is redacted from logs, traces, the debug overlay and error messages.
steps: Configure fixture sources using header-based authentication and assert no request URL contains the secret
Configure a fixture source that requires a key as a URL parameter
Trigger logging, tracing, the debug overlay (?debug=1) and a failing request, and assert the key appears in none of their outputs
Assert the sources guide explains how to keep secrets out of URLs

features.description: The engine keeps a live list of credits for the sources currently visible: it updates as sources enter and leave the view, removes duplicates, and is available through the public API and an event.
steps: Show two fixture sources with different attribution and coverage in the playground
Pan from one coverage area to the other while listening to the attribution event
Assert the credits list contains exactly the sources with visible tiles at each moment and the event fires on each change
Assert a source used by two layers is credited once

features.description: Even without the UI package, the engine shows a minimal attribution element with the required credits and logos of every visible source, and refuses configurations that would hide required attribution.
steps: Mount the engine without the UI package in a plain page with fixture sources that require attribution and a logo
Capture screenshots at several viewport sizes and assert the credits and logos are visible and not covered by any other element
Try to hide the attribution element through configuration and CSS and assert required credits stay visible and a warning names the requiring source
Assert sources that do not require attribution can be hidden from the element

features.description: An ADR records the reading of Google Maps Platform's current terms and Map Tiles API policies (including the separate EEA terms) and maps each rule to a setting of the Google profile.
steps: Open the Google terms ADR in docs/adr/ and confirm it records the date read and links to the terms, the Map Tiles API policies and the EEA terms
Confirm every rule that affects caching, prefetch, offline packaging, display-only use, logo and attribution placement and session tokens is mapped to a profile setting
Confirm the profile's code references the ADR and the conformance suite checks each mapped setting

features.description: The Google Maps Platform adapter shows Map Tiles API 2D tiles (roadmap, satellite, terrain) using the customer's own API key and session tokens, creating and renewing sessions automatically.
steps: Run the Google adapter conformance suite against a recorded fixture of the Map Tiles API (session creation, tiles, errors)
Assert a session is created with the configured map type, language and region, and tile requests carry the session token
Make the fixture expire the session and assert a new session is created transparently with zero black pixels

With the owner's API key, run the opt-in live test for roadmap, satellite and terrain and capture screenshots; without a key the fixture run is the pass condition and the pending live run is recorded in the open-questions file

features.description: Google attributions for the current viewport are requested from the Map Tiles API viewport information endpoint and shown, updated as the view changes.
steps: Show the Google fixture source in the playground and pan between areas with different fixture copyrights
Assert the viewport information request is made for each settled view and not on every frame
Assert the displayed attribution always matches the copyrights returned for the current viewport

features.description: When a Google source is visible, the Google logo and attributions are always visible and never covered, at every viewport size and with every UI control shown.
steps: Show the Google fixture source with the engine's built-in attribution element
Capture screenshots at desktop, tablet and phone viewport sizes in landscape and portrait
Assert through element hit-testing that the logo and attribution are fully visible and no other element overlaps them
Try to hide or cover them through configuration and app CSS and assert they stay visible

features.description: In-memory reuse of Google tiles respects the cache headers Google returns: tiles are reused only while their headers allow it.
steps: Serve Google fixture tiles with short Cache-Control lifetimes
Pan away and back before and after expiry
Assert tiles are reused from memory before expiry and requested again after expiry, with parent fallback and zero black pixels meanwhile

features.description: The Google profile applies the terms of the customer's billing region, including Google's separate EEA terms, as configured by the app.
steps: Configure the Google source with an EEA billing region and with a non-EEA billing region
Assert the effective profile settings match the respective rules recorded in the Google terms ADR
Assert a missing billing region produces a configuration error rather than a silent default

features.description: The Google adapter can request Street View metadata and panorama tiles through the Map Tiles API under the same profile (session token, attribution, no caching).
steps: Run the Street View part of the Google conformance suite against a recorded fixture (metadata and panorama tiles)
Assert requests carry the session token and panorama tiles are never persisted
Assert the attribution and logo rules of the Google profile apply wherever the tiles are displayed
With the owner's API key, run the opt-in live test; without a key the fixture run is the pass condition and the pending live run is recorded in the open-questions file

features.description: Live Google Maps Platform tests read a restricted API key only from the GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY environment variable or CI secret, never committed; they apply the EEA terms of the owner's billing region, stay within the free monthly usage caps, stop at the first quota error, and do not run when no key is set.
steps: Search the repository and its history for API key patterns and confirm no key is committed, and that the live tests read the key only from GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY
Run the live suite without the variable and confirm it reports that it did not run, while the fixture conformance suites still run and pass
Confirm the requests per live run, times the scheduled runs per month, stay below the free monthly cap of each Map Tiles API product recorded in the Google terms ADR
Make the fixture server answer with a quota error and confirm the live suite stops at once with a clear message
With the owner's key, run the live suite once and confirm it passes under the EEA terms

features.description: An ADR records the reading of the OpenStreetMap Foundation's current tile usage policy and maps each rule to a setting of the OpenStreetMap public-servers profile.
steps: Open the OpenStreetMap terms ADR in docs/adr/ and confirm it records the date read and links to the tile usage policy
Confirm every rule on bulk download, offline use, concurrency, application identification, caching headers and attribution is mapped to a profile setting
Confirm the profile's code references the ADR

features.description: The OpenStreetMap public-servers profile shows raster and vector tiles from the OpenStreetMap Foundation servers with attribution to OpenStreetMap contributors linked to the copyright page.
steps: Run the OpenStreetMap public adapter conformance suite against recorded fixtures of the raster and vector tile servers

Show the raster tiles in the playground and assert '© OpenStreetMap contributors' with a link to the OpenStreetMap copyright page is visible whenever they are; check the vector tiles through the MVT conformance suite (vector rendering arrives in M13)
Assert the profile honors the servers' cache headers and never sends no-cache request headers
Run the opt-in live test at low volume, as the policy allows

features.description: The OpenStreetMap public-servers profile keeps request concurrency to the low limit recorded in its ADR, during every navigation scenario.
steps: Run fast pan, zoom and flight scenarios with an OpenStreetMap public fixture source
Log open connections per host and assert they never exceed the profile's limit
Assert the view keeps showing parent-tile fallback with zero black pixels

features.description: The OpenStreetMap public-servers profile requires the application to identify itself as the usage policy requires, and sends that identification with every request.
steps: Configure the profile without an application identifier and assert configuration fails with a descriptive error
Configure it with an identifier and assert every request carries a valid Referer identifying the application (the referrer policy never strips it)
Assert the identification method matches the one recorded in the OpenStreetMap terms ADR

features.description: The OpenStreetMap public-servers profile is documented as unsuitable for production products, and the engine warns once in the console when it is used.
steps: Open the sources guide and confirm it states that the public OpenStreetMap servers are unsuitable for production and points to the self-hosted alternative
Use the profile in the playground and assert exactly one console warning is logged per engine instance

features.description: A guide for sources and custom adapters explains every built-in adapter, the adapter interface, writing and testing a custom adapter with the conformance suite, provider profiles, reprojection, layer composition and source chains, and why Apple map data is not supported.
steps: Open the sources guide in the documentation site and confirm each listed topic has a section with a working code example
Run the guide's code examples as tests and assert they pass
Confirm it explains that Apple map data may only be used through Apple's own MapKit and is therefore not offered

features.description: Milestone 7 acceptance: each adapter passes its conformance suite and a mixed stack switches sources without visible seams.
steps: Run the conformance suites of every built-in adapter, including the Google and OpenStreetMap profiles, and assert all pass
Open a playground scenario with a mixed imagery and terrain stack (offline package base, online detail chain, a reprojected UTM layer and a WMS overlay)
Record every frame during zoom, pan and flight across coverage boundaries on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Assert zero black pixels, no seams at source boundaries and no visible jump when the active source switches (frame-difference analysis)
Confirm no known bug remains open for this milestone
A fresh-context reviewer checks the milestone against PLAN.md and its acceptance criteria and reports no correctness or requirement gaps

features.description: A written research survey on offline use, persistent browser storage and network adaptation exists in docs/research/, covering how the studied engines and adaptive streaming players handle caches, packages, connectivity and bandwidth, their known failure modes, and the chosen approach.
steps: Open the offline survey in docs/research/ and confirm it covers CesiumJS, MapLibre GL JS and MapLibre Native offline packs, OpenLayers, PMTiles tooling and adaptive bitrate techniques from video streaming
Confirm it compares IndexedDB, OPFS and the Cache API (quotas, eviction, performance, browser support including Safari)
Confirm it lists known failure modes from issue trackers (quota errors, browser eviction, captive portals, stale caches) and how the chosen design avoids each
Confirm it states the chosen approach and why and links the ADRs that record it

features.description: With no configuration, the network mode is hybrid and every loading feature (persistent cache, memory reuse, prefetch and flight preloading, offline packaging) is enabled.
steps: Create an engine with no network or cache options in a Vitest test and in the playground
Read the effective settings through the public API and assert the network mode is hybrid and every loading feature is on
Navigate the playground and assert tiles are persisted, reused from memory, prefetched around the view and packageable

features.description: Tiles come from the first cache tier that holds them, in the order GPU, RAM, persistent browser storage, offline packages, network, and each tier is filled on the way back.
steps: Instrument per-tier hit counters (also shown in the debug overlay, ?debug=1)
Load a view from the network, pan away until tiles leave GPU memory, then come back, then reload the page, then clear storage with a package installed
Assert each revisit is served by the expected tier and makes no request to a lower tier
Assert no tile is ever downloaded twice while a higher tier still holds it

features.description: The persistent cache stores tiles in browser storage (IndexedDB or OPFS) across sessions, so revisiting an area after a page reload makes no network request for cached tiles.
steps: Navigate a fixture area in the playground, then reload the page and navigate the same path
Assert through request interception that no cached tile is requested again
Assert writes and reads happen off the main thread and frame times stay within budget during heavy cache writes
Repeat in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit

features.description: Storage quotas are handled: when the persistent cache reaches its configured size or the browser quota, least-recently-used tiles are evicted and quota errors never crash the engine or blank the view.
steps: Configure a small persistent cache size and navigate until it is exceeded, and assert least-recently-used tiles are evicted and the size stays within the limit
Inject QuotaExceededError on writes and assert the engine logs one warning, keeps rendering with zero black pixels, and keeps working from memory and network
Assert storage use reported by the API matches the stored data within 5%

features.description: When the browser evicts the engine's stored tiles or packages, the engine detects it and falls back to the remaining tiers without errors or blank views, and reports it through an event.
steps: Install a package and fill the persistent cache, then delete the browser storage while the page is open and between sessions
Navigate and assert the engine falls back to network or lower-detail tiers with zero black pixels after the base is available
Assert an eviction event reports which packages or caches were lost

features.description: Apps can request persistent storage from the browser through the engine's API and read whether it was granted.
steps: Call the request-persistence API in the playground in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit
Assert it calls navigator.storage.persist() and reports the browser's answer and the current persisted state
Assert the call is safe where the Storage API is missing and reports 'unsupported'

features.description: The cache respects each source's cache policy: Cache-Control and Expires headers decide how long tiles are reused, and tiles marked no-store are never persisted.
steps: Serve fixture tiles with max-age, no-cache, no-store and Expires headers
Navigate, wait past expiry and navigate again
Assert fresh tiles are reused without requests, expired tiles are revalidated, and no-store tiles are absent from browser storage
Assert per-source policy overrides in configuration can only shorten what the headers and profile allow

features.description: Changed data is detected through ETags: expired tiles are revalidated with If-None-Match, a 304 response reuses the stored tile, and changed tiles replace the stored ones.
steps: Serve fixture tiles with ETags, let them expire, then change some of them on the server
Navigate again and assert revalidation requests carry If-None-Match
Assert unchanged tiles get 304 and are reused, and changed tiles are downloaded and replace the stored ones without a visible flash

features.description: Offline packages are versioned, and installing a new version invalidates the tiles of the old one.
steps: Install version 1 of a fixture package and navigate it
Install version 2 with some changed tiles and navigate again
Assert every tile shown comes from version 2 and no stale version-1 tile remains in memory or browser storage

features.description: With the persistent cache switched off, the engine neither reads from nor writes to browser storage for tile caching.
steps: Switch the persistent cache off globally and navigate a fixture area, then reload and navigate again
Assert through storage inspection that no tile was written and through request interception that revisited tiles are downloaded again
Switch it off for one source only and assert the other sources still persist

features.description: With memory reuse on, recently used tiles stay in RAM and GPU memory after they leave the screen, within the memory budgets, so panning back shows them without requests.
steps: Pan away from a loaded area and back within the memory budget
Assert returning tiles are drawn from memory on the first frame with no request and no black pixels
Assert GPU and RAM use stay within the configured budgets with least-recently-used eviction

features.description: With memory reuse off, only the working set needed to draw the current view stays in RAM and GPU memory, released as soon as it is off screen.
steps: Switch memory reuse off and pan across a fixture area
Assert GPU and RAM tile memory track the current working set and drop after tiles leave the screen
Pan back and assert tiles come from persistent storage, packages or network, with parent fallback and zero black pixels

features.description: Disabling every cache feature never means zero memory: tiles on screen stay in GPU memory while visible and the view never flickers or blanks.
steps: Switch off persistent cache, memory reuse and prefetch and hold the camera still, then pan slowly
Record every frame and assert no visible tile is evicted and re-requested while on screen
Assert zero black pixels and no flicker (frame-difference analysis)

features.description: With prefetch on, tiles just outside the view (around it and the next detail level) load before they become visible, at lower priority than visible tiles.
steps: Hold the camera still until the view is complete, then pan by half a screen at normal speed
Assert tiles entering the view were already loaded and are drawn at full detail on the first frame they appear
Assert prefetch requests are issued only after all visible tiles are requested and are cancelled when the view moves away

features.description: With prefetch and flight preloading off, the engine requests only tiles needed for the current view.
steps: Switch prefetch and flight preloading off and run pan and flight scenarios with request interception
Assert every request is for a tile that was visible when requested
Switch them off for one source only and assert the other sources still prefetch

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: When a flight starts, the destination is loaded at the levels needed on arrival, so the arrival view is complete with no black pixels and no popping.
steps: Run a Milan to Tokyo flight scenario (?scenario=flight-milan-tokyo) against fixture servers with 100 ms latency
Assert destination tiles at the arrival levels are requested right after the flight starts
Record frames during the final descent and arrival and assert zero black pixels and no popping (frame-difference analysis)
Repeat on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Along a flight path, the engine loads only what will actually be visible, at the detail the moving camera can show.
steps: Run long flight scenarios with request interception and record which requested tiles were ever drawn
Assert at least 95% of the tiles requested along the path (destination preloads excluded) are drawn before the flight ends
Assert no tile is requested at a finer level than the motion-aware detail allows for the camera speed at that moment

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Detail is motion-aware: during fast motion the engine accepts coarser levels, and it refines to full detail when the camera slows down or stops.
steps: Run a fast pan scenario and a slow pan scenario over the same area with request logging
Assert fewer and coarser tiles are requested during the fast pan, with frame times within budget
Stop the camera and assert full detail is reached and transitions cross-fade without popping
Assert the coarsening never leaves black pixels

features.description: The offline-packaging switch decides, globally or per source, whether a source's tiles may be included in offline packages.
steps: Switch offline packaging off for one fixture source and build a package covering that source and another one
Assert the package contains only the other source's tiles and the build report states why the first one was excluded
Switch it off globally and assert package builds are refused with a descriptive error

features.description: Every network and loading switch can be set globally, overridden per layer, and changed at runtime without a reload and without a visible glitch.
steps: Toggle each switch globally and per layer through the public API while a pan scenario runs
Assert each change takes effect within one frame for new requests, as observed through request interception and storage inspection
Record frames during each toggle and assert zero black pixels and no flicker

features.description: In online-only mode the engine never reads offline packages, even when they are installed.
steps: Install a fixture package and set the network mode to online only (?network=online)
Navigate the package's area and assert no tile is read from the package (per-tier counters) and all come from the network or caches
Block the network and assert the engine reports that it is offline, keeps the pinned base visible and does not read the package

features.description: In offline-only mode the engine never touches the network: no tile requests and no health checks, suitable for air-gapped sites.
steps: Set the network mode to offline only (?network=offline) with installed packages and cached tiles
Run zoom, pan and flight scenarios while recording every network request at the browser level
Assert zero network requests are made, health checks included
Assert full navigation works from packages and caches with zero black pixels inside package coverage

features.description: Hybrid mode (the default) uses offline packages and the network together, picking for each tile the best source it can get without causing lag.
steps: Set the network mode to hybrid (?network=hybrid) with a low-detail fixture package and an online fixture source
Run zoom and flight scenarios and assert coarse levels come from the package and fine levels from the network
Assert frame times stay within budget and zero black pixels appear

features.description: Mixed mode gives an instant start and smooth flights from a fixed low-detail package, while higher detail loads online on demand.
steps: Start the playground in hybrid mode with a world low-detail fixture package and a throttled online source (400 kbps, 300 ms latency)
Measure the time to the first complete frame and assert it meets the first-frame target with no network tile needed
Run a long flight and assert intermediate views come from the package with zero black pixels and frame times within budget
Assert detail beyond the package arrives from the network after the camera settles

features.description: Offline mode 1: with no internet and the network mode set to hybrid, the engine reads offline packages and static tile folders served over HTTP by a server on the local network.
steps: Serve fixture PMTiles and MBTiles packages and a static tile folder from a local static HTTP server, set the network mode to hybrid and block every other host
Run zoom, pan and flight scenarios and assert full navigation with zero black pixels inside package coverage
Assert the first complete frame arrives within 1 s on the LAN setup
Assert health checks target only the LAN endpoints and the engine never waits on unreachable internet hosts

features.description: Offline mode 2: with no network at all, the engine runs from packages and cached tiles stored in the browser.
steps: Install a fixture package into browser storage and fill the persistent cache, then emulate a fully offline browser with Playwright
Reload the playground and run zoom, pan and flight scenarios
Assert full navigation within package coverage with zero black pixels and no failed requests visible to the user

features.description: Connectivity is detected with health checks against the tile endpoints, not the browser's online flag alone, so captive portals and dead endpoints are recognized as offline.
steps: Simulate a captive portal: navigator.onLine is true but tile endpoints return a redirect or an HTML login page
Assert the engine reports the endpoints as unreachable, does not use the portal responses as tiles, and falls back to packages and caches
Simulate a single dead endpoint while others work and assert only that endpoint is marked unreachable
Assert health checks back off while offline and never exceed one request per endpoint per configured interval

features.description: When connectivity drops, the engine switches seamlessly to packages and caches: no black areas, no error flood, no request storm.
steps: Cut the network in the middle of a pan scenario and a flight scenario
Record every frame and assert zero black pixels where packages or caches cover the view, parent fallback elsewhere, and no flicker
Assert pending requests are cancelled and no retries are made until a health check succeeds
Assert a connectivity event reports the change

features.description: When connectivity returns, the engine resumes online detail seamlessly: refined tiles cross-fade in without jumps or popping.
steps: Restore the network during a held view and during a pan scenario
Assert a health check detects the change and online requests resume for the visible view first
Record frames and assert refinement cross-fades with no popping and no black pixels
Assert a connectivity event reports the change

features.description: Throughput is estimated from measured tile downloads, so bandwidth adaptation works in every browser, including Firefox and Safari where the Network Information API is missing.
steps: Throttle fixture servers to 400 kbps, 5 Mbps and 50 Mbps in turn and navigate
Assert the engine's bandwidth estimate (also shown in the debug overlay) converges within 20% of the throttled throughput within 10 s
Repeat in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit and assert the estimate does not depend on the Network Information API

features.description: The bandwidth estimate sets the maximum detail loaded during flights, so flights stay smooth on slow links and use full detail on fast ones.
steps: Run the same long flight at 400 kbps and at 50 Mbps
Assert the finest level requested during the flight is lower on the slow link and that both runs keep frame times within budget with zero black pixels
Assert the arrival view refines to full detail on both links

features.description: The bandwidth estimate sets the prefetch depth: more prefetch on fast links, less on slow links, so prefetch never delays visible tiles.
steps: Run the same pan scenario at 400 kbps and at 50 Mbps with prefetch on
Assert the number of prefetched tiles is larger on the fast link
Assert on the slow link visible tiles are never queued behind prefetch requests

features.description: The bandwidth estimate sets request concurrency within each host's and profile's limits, raising it on fast links and lowering it on slow or high-latency links.
steps: Run a zoom scenario on links with 400 kbps, 50 Mbps and 500 ms latency
Log concurrent requests per host and assert concurrency adapts to each link and never exceeds the host or profile limits
Assert the time to a complete view is no worse than with the best fixed concurrency for that link by more than 10%

features.description: The offline package builder takes a bounding box, a zoom range and sources whose licenses allow it, and outputs a PMTiles package.
steps: Run the package builder CLI from the tools package with a bounding box around Rome, zooms 0 to 14 and a fixture source
Assert the output is a valid PMTiles archive containing exactly the tiles of that area and zoom range
Load the package in the playground in offline-only mode and assert full navigation of the area with zero black pixels

features.description: The offline package builder also accepts a polygon area and can output an MBTiles package.
steps: Run the package builder with a polygon outlining a region and MBTiles output
Assert the package contains every tile intersecting the polygon and no tile entirely outside it
Load the package in the playground in offline-only mode and assert navigation within the polygon with zero black pixels

features.description: Every offline package records the license and attribution of its sources, and the engine shows that attribution when the package's tiles are visible.
steps: Build a package from two fixture sources with different licenses and attribution
Assert the package metadata lists each source's license and attribution
Load it in the playground and assert the attribution shown matches the package metadata for the visible tiles

features.description: The package builder estimates tile count and size before building, accounting for each extra zoom level roughly quadrupling the tile count.
steps: Run the size estimate for several areas and zoom ranges
Assert the tile count is exact for the given area and range and the byte estimate is within 25% of the built package
Assert the estimate is shown before any tile is downloaded and the user can cancel

features.description: Package downloads are resumable: an interrupted build or install continues where it stopped without downloading completed tiles again.
steps: Interrupt a package build halfway (kill the process) and an in-browser package install (close the page)
