Resume each and assert already completed tiles are not requested again
Assert the final package is identical to an uninterrupted build

features.description: Packages carry integrity checks, verified when they are installed and read, so corrupted packages are detected and never shown as corrupted imagery.
steps: Corrupt bytes in a fixture package header, directory and tile data in turn
Install and read each and assert corruption is detected with a descriptive error
Assert corrupted tiles are treated as missing, with parent fallback and zero black pixels

features.description: Partial packages (missing tiles or levels, truncated downloads) are handled gracefully: available tiles are used and the gaps are covered by ancestors or other sources.
steps: Install fixture packages with missing levels, missing tiles and a truncated last chunk
Navigate them in offline-only mode and record frames
Assert available tiles are shown, gaps are covered by the best ancestor or the next source in the chain, and no frame is blank or frozen

features.description: The package management API installs packages from a URL or a file, with progress events, and lists installed packages with their metadata.
steps: Install a fixture package from a URL and another from a local file in the playground
Assert progress events are emitted and the list API returns both with name, version, area, zoom range, sources, licenses and size
Reload the page and assert the list is unchanged

features.description: The package management API updates a package to a new version and removes packages, freeing their storage.
steps: Update an installed fixture package to a new version and assert the list shows the new version and only its tiles are used
Remove a package and assert it disappears from the list, its storage is freed, and the view falls back to other tiers without black pixels

features.description: Apps can read storage use: per package, for the persistent cache, in total, and the browser quota.
steps: Install packages and fill the cache in the playground
Call the storage-use API and assert per-package, cache and total sizes match the stored data within 5% and the quota is reported when the browser provides it

features.description: Every combination of network mode (online only, offline only, hybrid) and loading-feature switch (persistent cache, memory reuse, prefetch and flight preloading, offline packaging), with and without a restrictive provider profile, in both offline setups, behaves as specified.
steps: Run an automated matrix of all 3 x 2^4 combinations, each with an unrestricted source and a source with a restrictive profile
For each combination, run a short zoom, pan and flight scenario with request interception and storage inspection
Run the combinations that involve packages in both offline setups (LAN server and browser storage)
Assert requests, storage reads and writes, memory residency and packaging behavior match the specification and the profile rules for every combination
Assert zero black pixels after the base has loaded in every combination where the base is reachable

features.description: A network simulation suite runs the navigation scenarios on offline, slow, flaky and high-latency links and in LAN-only mode.
steps: Run the network suite with Playwright: fully offline, 400 kbps, flaky (20% of requests dropped or reset), 500 ms latency, and LAN-only
Assert each scenario completes with zero black pixels after the base has loaded, no popping, and frame times within budget
Assert no request is retried endlessly and every failed request backs off
Assert the suite runs in CI

features.description: There is no telemetry: during every scenario the engine sends requests only to the configured sources and the configured asset URLs.
steps: Record every network request at the browser level during the full scenario suite with all features enabled
Assert every request targets a configured source, package or health-check endpoint, or a configured worker or asset URL
Assert no request carries data about the user or the view beyond what a tile request needs

features.description: A guide for offline packages explains network modes, loading switches, both offline setups, building packages with the CLI, the management API, storage quotas and persistence.
steps: Open the offline guide in the documentation site and confirm each listed topic has a section with a working example
Run the guide's code examples as tests and assert they pass
Follow the LAN server setup in the guide on a clean machine and confirm the playground runs offline from it

features.description: Adapters declare each provider's rules, and the engine never stores a source's tiles in persistent storage when those rules forbid caching.
steps: Configure a fixture source whose declared rules forbid persistent caching, with the global persistent cache on
Navigate the playground through a zoom and pan scenario
Inspect browser storage through Playwright and assert no tile of that source was written
Assert tiles of the other sources in the same view were written

features.description: The engine refuses to include a source in an offline package when its declared rules forbid offline packaging.
steps: Request a package that includes a fixture source whose rules forbid offline packaging through the package builder
Assert the build stops before any download with an error naming the source and the rule
Assert the same package without that source builds normally

features.description: Provider profiles follow one rule: every feature is enabled by default, a profile switches off only what its provider forbids and only for its own source, developers can switch off more globally or per source, and nothing can switch on what a profile forbids.
steps: Configure a fixture source with a profile forbidding persistent cache and prefetch, next to an unrestricted source
Assert the unrestricted source has every loading feature enabled and the restricted one has only the forbidden ones disabled
Switch off memory reuse for the restricted source and prefetch globally, and assert both take effect
Try to switch on persistent cache for the restricted source globally and per source, and assert it stays off and a warning names the profile rule
Unit-test the effective-settings resolution for every combination of global setting, per-source setting and profile rule

features.description: The Google profile allows no persistent caching and no offline packaging of Google content beyond what Google's terms and cache headers allow, whatever the global settings.
steps: Enable persistent cache and offline packaging globally and navigate a Google fixture source
Inspect browser storage and assert no Google tile is persisted beyond what the Google terms ADR allows
Request an offline package with the Google source and assert it is refused with an error naming the Google profile

features.description: The Google profile limits prefetch and flight preloading of Google content to what Google's terms allow.
steps: Enable prefetch and flight preloading globally and run a pan scenario and a long flight with a Google fixture source
Assert through request interception that Google tiles are requested only within the limits recorded in the Google terms ADR
Assert other sources in the same view still prefetch and preload normally

features.description: Google content is used for display only: data-access APIs (tile data, pixel readback, elevation sampling and export of Google content) refuse Google sources.
steps: Call each data-access API (tile data access, pixel readback, elevation sampling, package export) on a Google fixture source
Assert each call is refused with an error naming the Google profile rule

features.description: The OpenStreetMap public-servers profile forbids offline packaging and bulk prefetch, whatever the global settings.
steps: Enable prefetch, flight preloading and offline packaging globally with an OpenStreetMap public fixture source
Run a pan and a long flight scenario and assert prefetch and flight preloading of its tiles stay within the limits recorded in the OpenStreetMap terms ADR (no bulk prefetch)
Request an offline package with the source and assert it is refused with an error naming the profile rule

features.description: The OpenStreetMap self-hosted or provider profile enables every feature, shows the ODbL attribution, and applies a commercial provider's own profile on top when one is used.
steps: Configure a self-hosted OpenStreetMap fixture source and assert persistent cache, memory reuse, prefetch, flight preloading and offline packaging are all enabled
Assert '© OpenStreetMap contributors' with ODbL licensing is shown whenever its tiles are visible
Configure the same data through a fixture provider profile with its own restrictions and assert both the ODbL attribution and the provider's rules apply

features.description: Any other provider's adapter can declare its own profile, and the engine enforces it exactly as it enforces the built-in Google and OpenStreetMap profiles.
steps: Write a fixture provider adapter that declares a profile forbidding persistent cache and offline packaging, requiring a logo and limiting concurrency
Run the shared conformance suite's profile-enforcement checks against it
Assert each declared rule is enforced in the playground exactly as for the built-in profiles

features.description: Persistent cache stores and network policies are public extension points: an application can plug in its own cache store or network policy without changing engine code, and the built-in implementations pass the same contract tests.
steps: Create a test package outside packages/ with a custom cache store and a custom network policy written against the public interfaces
Run the cache-store and network-policy contract tests against the built-in implementations and the custom ones and assert all pass
Attach the custom store and policy in the playground and assert tiles are stored and requests decided through them

features.description: PMTiles and MBTiles packages containing terrain (quantized-mesh or heightmap) and Mapbox Vector Tiles load through the package adapters over HTTP, from a file and from browser storage, so terrain and vector layers work in both offline modes and are cached like imagery.
steps: Build fixture packages with terrain and vector tiles and serve them from a LAN-style server, a local file and browser storage
Run the terrain and MVT conformance checks against each package source and assert identical tiles
Navigate the playground offline over the package area and assert terrain relief appears with zero black pixels
Assert terrain and vector tiles are written to and read from the persistent cache like imagery tiles

features.description: A Docker-based static LAN server script lets any machine play the offline local-network role: one command serves the playground build, engine assets and offline packages over HTTP on the local network with the headers the engine needs, and the offline mode 1 tests use it.
steps: Run the LAN server script on a machine with only Docker and confirm it serves the playground, the engine assets and a fixture package on the configured port
Confirm the responses carry correct MIME types, CORS and caching headers and support HTTP range requests for PMTiles
From another machine or container on the same network with no internet route, open the playground and confirm offline navigation with zero black pixels
Confirm the offline mode 1 end-to-end tests start the same server image

features.description: Milestone 8 acceptance: the network scenarios pass (offline, slow, flaky, connection dropping and returning), and every combination of network mode and loading-feature switch behaves as specified.
steps: Run the network simulation suite, the connectivity drop and return scenarios, and both offline setups and assert all pass
Run the full network-mode by loading-switch matrix and assert every combination passes
Record frames for each scenario on WebGPU and forced WebGL2 and assert zero black pixels after the base has loaded and no popping
Confirm no known bug remains open for this milestone
A fresh-context reviewer checks the milestone against PLAN.md and its acceptance criteria and reports no correctness or requirement gaps

features.description: The research survey on terrain, imagery and vector tile generation tools (quantized-mesh tooling, Martini and Delatin, PMTiles tooling, GDAL-based pipelines) is written in docs/research/ with the chosen pipeline approach justified.
steps: Open the data pipeline survey in docs/research/
Verify it explains how the quantized-mesh tools, Martini, Delatin, the PMTiles tools and GDAL-based pipelines generate terrain, imagery and vector tiles, based on their code
Verify it lists correctness, seam, performance and reproducibility issues from their issue trackers, with links
Verify it states the chosen pipeline approach and why, linking the ADR

features.description: The tools package provides a TypeScript command-line pipeline that downloads, converts and tiles each default dataset from versioned configuration files, calling GDAL and other external tools through a Docker image pinned by digest.
steps: Run the pipeline CLI help and verify it exposes download, convert, tile, estimate and package commands for every default dataset
Run a build for a small test region from a configuration file committed in the repository
Verify GDAL and every other external tool run inside a Docker image pinned by digest, with nothing needed on the host beyond Node and Docker
Run `npm test` and verify the pipeline's unit tests (configuration validation, tile math, build planning) pass

features.description: The license and attribution terms of every default dataset are re-verified against the current official pages before shipping and recorded in an ADR.
steps: Open the default-data license ADR in docs/adr/

Verify it records, with reading date and source link, the current terms of Copernicus DEM GLO-30, Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX, the global fallback raster, OpenStreetMap (ODbL) and raw Copernicus Sentinel-2 data
Verify each dataset is confirmed as free for commercial use and redistribution, with its exact required attribution text
Run the automated consistency check and verify the pipeline configuration files use the attribution text recorded in the ADR

features.description: The pipeline refuses to download or package any source whose terms forbid offline packaging or redistribution, before writing any output.
steps: Configure builds that include a forbidden source: the Sentinel-2 cloudless 2018 or later edition, the public OpenStreetMap tile servers, and a source under the Google Maps Platform profile
Run each build and verify it stops before any download with an error naming the source and the term it violates
Verify no partial output folder or package is left behind
Run the unit tests of the license gate against every built-in provider profile and verify allowed and forbidden cases

features.description: Before building, the pipeline estimates tile count and output size per dataset, region and zoom level, showing that each extra zoom level roughly quadruples the tile count.
steps: Run the estimate command for the world low-detail configuration and for the Italy high-detail configuration
Verify the output lists tile counts and estimated bytes per dataset, region and zoom level, plus totals
Verify tile counts grow by about 4x per added zoom level for a fixed area
Build a small region and verify the actual output size is within 30% of the estimate

features.description: Before downloading anything, the pipeline prints the estimated download size, output size and cost (including AWS requester-pays transfer) of the build and asks for confirmation; it proceeds only after an explicit yes, or an explicit confirmation flag in non-interactive runs.
steps: Run a sample-area build interactively and confirm the estimate is printed before any request to a data source and the build waits for confirmation
Answer no and confirm nothing is downloaded or written
Run the same build non-interactively without the confirmation flag and confirm it stops before any download
Confirm the cost estimate uses per-GB prices recorded in the pipeline configuration with their reading date, and the actual transfer of the sample build is within 30% of the estimate

features.description: Interrupted builds resume where they stopped without redoing completed work, and integrity checks detect and regenerate corrupted downloads or tiles.
steps: Start a dataset build and kill the process midway through downloading and again midway through tiling
Restart the build and verify from the log that completed downloads and tiles are skipped
Verify the resumed output is identical by checksum to an uninterrupted build of the same configuration
Corrupt one downloaded source file and one intermediate tile, rerun, and verify both are detected by checksum and regenerated

features.description: Every build can output both offline packages (PMTiles or MBTiles) and static tile folders ready for any HTTP server or CDN.
steps: Run a build with both package and static-folder outputs enabled
Serve the static folder with a plain static HTTP server and load it in the playground through the XYZ adapter
Load the package through the PMTiles or MBTiles adapter and verify a sample of tiles is byte-identical to the static folder
Verify the package passes the offline package integrity check

features.description: Every pipeline output records its sources' license and attribution in machine-readable metadata, which the engine reads to show the required credits.
steps: Build any default dataset and inspect the package metadata and the static folder's metadata file
Verify license identifier, attribution text, source links, data year, configuration version and pipeline version are present
Load the output in the playground and verify the attribution shows the recorded text while its tiles are visible

features.description: A very low resolution whole-world fallback imagery pyramid is built from Natural Earth raster data (public domain) or an equivalent license-compatible source.
steps: Run the global fallback build from its configuration
Verify every tile of every built level exists and covers the whole world, including the polar regions
Load it as the pinned base in the playground and capture screenshots of the globe from several directions: zero black or empty pixels on the globe
Verify the output's license metadata states its public-domain or equivalent status

features.description: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 is downloaded from AWS Open Data and converted into terrain tiles that the engine's terrain adapter loads with correct relief.
steps: Run the DEM build for a mountainous test region (for example the Alps around Mont Blanc) from its configuration
Verify source tiles come from the public Copernicus DEM AWS Open Data bucket and are checksummed
Compare heights sampled from the output at 1,000 random points against the source DEM: error within the documented quantization tolerance of the tile format
Load the output in the playground through the terrain adapter and verify relief displays with no cracks on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Verify the output attribution includes the Copernicus DEM notice with the modification statement

features.description: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX is converted from its original tiles into a self-hosted imagery tile pyramid, and only the commercially usable 2016 edition is accepted.
steps: Run the Sentinel-2 cloudless build for a test region using the owner's requester-pays credentials, or the documented fixture stub when credentials are not yet available
Verify the pipeline rejects the 2018 and later editions with an explicit non-commercial license error
Load the pyramid in the playground and verify imagery displays at about 10 m per pixel at the highest level, with no seams between source tiles
Verify the output carries the EOX and Copernicus attribution text recorded in the license ADR

features.description: OpenStreetMap extracts are downloaded from an extract provider (for example Geofabrik) and converted into self-hosted Mapbox Vector Tiles with roads, places and buildings, never fetched from the public OpenStreetMap tile servers.
steps: Run the OSM build for a small extract from its configuration
Record network traffic and verify downloads come only from the configured extract provider, with no request to any public OpenStreetMap tile server
Validate the output tiles with the engine's MVT adapter conformance suite
Verify road, place and building layers exist, with building height and level attributes preserved where present
Verify the output attribution credits OpenStreetMap contributors under the ODbL

features.description: Builds are region-based: the whole world at low detail and chosen regions, Italy first, at high detail, each defined only by configuration.
steps: Run the world low-detail configuration and the Italy high-detail configuration for every default dataset
Verify the world output stops at its configured maximum zoom and the Italy output covers the Italian territory polygon up to its configured high zoom

Load the imagery and terrain outputs in the playground as source chains, zoom into Italy and across its borders, and verify high detail inside Italy with seamless fallback outside (zero black pixels, no visible seam); check the OpenStreetMap vector-tile outputs with the MVT conformance suite
Add a new test region with only a new configuration file and verify it builds without code changes

features.description: Builds are region-based and defined only by configuration: the repository ships ready-to-run configurations for the world at low detail and for Italy at high detail, verified on small sample areas, which consumers run in full on their own infrastructure and AWS account.
steps: Open the world low-detail and Italy high-detail configurations and confirm they cover every default dataset with their extents, zoom ranges and outputs
Run each configuration restricted to its documented sample area and confirm the outputs stop at the configured zooms and cover the sample area

Load the sample outputs in the playground as source chains, zoom across the high-detail boundary and confirm high detail inside with seamless fallback outside (zero black pixels, no visible seam); check the OpenStreetMap vector-tile outputs with the MVT conformance suite
Run the estimate command on both full configurations and confirm it completes without downloading anything
Add a new test region with only a new configuration file and confirm it builds without code changes

features.description: Rebuilding a dataset from the same versioned configuration produces identical output.
steps: Verify each configuration pins source dataset versions, tool versions and Docker image digests
Build the same configuration twice in clean directories
Compare both outputs by checksum and verify tiles and metadata are identical

features.description: The engine's default configuration uses only the self-hosted free default datasets and makes no request to Google, Apple, Mapbox, MapTiler, Cesium ion or any other paid or restricted service.
steps: Start the playground with the default configuration pointing at a local static server holding the default datasets
Record every network request during a scripted globe-to-street session
Assert every request targets the configured self-hosted origin
Scan the built packages' default configuration and bundles for hosts of paid or restricted services and verify none is referenced outside optional adapters

features.description: A data licenses and attributions document lists every default and optional dataset with its license, required attribution, source and re-verification date.
steps: Open the data licenses document in docs/
Verify every default dataset and the optional Sentinel-2 mosaic are listed with license, attribution text, source link and re-verification date
Run the automated check and verify the document matches the license metadata emitted by the pipeline

features.section: Working method for a multi-session build
features.description: A Claude Code skill documents and drives the dataset-build workflow: estimate, build, resume, verify and publish.
steps: Open the dataset-build skill under .claude/skills/
Verify it covers size estimation, building from configuration, resuming, integrity and license checks, and publishing outputs
Follow the skill's steps for a small test region end to end and verify they work exactly as written

features.description: A hosting guide shows consumers how to serve tiles, offline packages and engine assets from their own backend and frontend (a static HTTP server, object storage behind a CDN, or a LAN server), since the project runs no servers.
steps: Open the hosting guide in the documentation site and confirm it covers static folders, PMTiles and MBTiles packages, engine assets served from the app's own origin with a configurable base path, MIME types, CORS, HTTP range requests, caching and compression headers, and attribution
Follow the guide to host the sample outputs and engine assets with a plain static server and confirm the playground runs from them
Confirm the guide and the default configuration reference no server run by the project

features.description: Milestone 9 acceptance: the default datasets rebuild reproducibly from configuration.
steps: From a clean checkout, run the world low-detail and Italy high-detail builds of every default dataset from configuration (the Sentinel-2 2016 step runs on the sample area when the owner's requester-pays credentials are unavailable, recorded in the open-questions file)
Verify the outputs are identical by checksum to a previous build of the same configuration

Load the imagery and terrain outputs in the playground both as static folders and as offline packages and run a globe-to-street scenario over Italy: zero black pixels on WebGPU and forced WebGL2; check the vector-tile outputs with the MVT conformance suite
Verify license and attribution metadata accompany every output and match the data licenses document
Confirm no known bug remains open for this milestone
A fresh-context reviewer checks the milestone against PLAN.md and its acceptance criteria and reports no correctness or requirement gaps

features.description: Milestone 9 acceptance: the default datasets rebuild reproducibly from configuration on the sample areas, and the world and Italy configurations are ready to run.
steps: From a clean checkout, run the world low-detail and Italy high-detail configurations of every default dataset on their documented sample areas
Verify the outputs are identical by checksum to a previous build of the same configuration

Load the imagery and terrain outputs in the playground both as static folders and as offline packages and run a globe-to-street scenario over the Italian sample area: zero black pixels on WebGPU and forced WebGL2; check the vector-tile outputs with the MVT conformance suite
Verify license and attribution metadata accompany every output and match the data licenses document
Run the estimate for both full configurations and confirm size and cost are printed with no download
Confirm no known bug remains open for this milestone
A fresh-context reviewer checks the milestone against PLAN.md and its acceptance criteria and reports no correctness or requirement gaps

features.description: The picking research survey is written in docs/research/: approaches, trade-offs, known failure modes from issue trackers, tests and benchmarks studied, and the chosen approach with reasons.
steps: Open the picking survey in docs/research/
Verify it studies at least CesiumJS, MapLibre GL JS, deck.gl, three.js, OpenLayers and iTowns, covering GPU id-buffer picking, ray casting and CPU spatial indices
Verify it lists known failure modes with issue references (for example missed picks on terrain, precision at street level, picking cost per frame, picking during motion)
Verify it states the chosen approach, why it matches or beats the studied engines, and how it will be tested

features.description: The labels research survey is written in docs/research/: approaches, trade-offs, known failure modes from issue trackers, tests and benchmarks studied, and the chosen approach with reasons.
steps: Open the labels survey in docs/research/

Verify it studies at least MapLibre GL JS, MapLibre Native, Tangram, CesiumJS, OpenLayers and deck.gl, covering glyph generation (signed distance fields), atlases, collision indices, placement and fading
Verify it lists known failure modes with issue references (for example blurry text, flicker during motion, collision jitter, missing glyphs, cost of re-placement)
Verify it states the chosen approach, why, and how it will be tested

features.description: The research survey on data-layer primitives, terrain draping and ground clamping, clustering and massive point datasets (including Potree and deck.gl) is written in docs/research/ with the chosen approach justified.
steps: Open the data layers survey in docs/research/

Verify it explains how CesiumJS, deck.gl, MapLibre GL JS, OpenLayers, iTowns and Potree render primitives, drape and clamp them on terrain, cluster markers and handle massive point datasets, based on their code
Verify it lists draping, clamping, clustering and large-dataset performance issues from their issue trackers, with links
Verify it summarizes how those projects test and benchmark data layers
Verify it states the chosen approach and why, linking the ADR

features.description: Point primitives render at their exact positions with configurable pixel size, color and outline in the globe, 2D and tilted 3D phases.
steps: Open `?scenario=data-points` with 1,000 points spread worldwide
Capture screenshots in the globe, 2D map and tilted 3D phases on WebGPU and forced WebGL2 and compare against baselines within tolerance
Verify each point's screen position matches its projected coordinate within 1 pixel
Verify points on the far side of the globe are hidden by horizon culling

features.description: Markers and billboards show images facing the screen, with configurable anchor, size, rotation and pixel offset, crisp on high-DPI screens.
steps: Open `?scenario=data-markers` with markers using several images, anchors, sizes, rotations and offsets
Capture screenshots on WebGPU and forced WebGL2 at device pixel ratio 1 and 2 and compare against baselines within tolerance
Rotate and tilt the camera and verify billboards keep facing the screen and the anchor stays on the coordinate within 1 pixel
Verify marker images share a texture atlas so draw calls stay within the documented budget

features.description: Polylines render with configurable pixel width, color and opacity, and long segments follow the ellipsoid surface instead of cutting through the globe.
steps: Open `?scenario=data-lines` with short lines, intercontinental lines and lines of several widths
Capture screenshots in the globe, 2D and tilted 3D phases on WebGPU and forced WebGL2 and compare against baselines within tolerance
Verify an intercontinental line stays on the globe surface in the globe phase (no segment passes below the surface)
Verify line width stays constant in pixels while zooming and joins show no gaps or spikes at sharp angles

features.description: Polygons, including polygons with holes and very large polygons, render with fill color, opacity and outline in every phase.
steps: Open `?scenario=data-polygons` with small polygons, polygons with holes and a continent-sized polygon
Capture screenshots in the globe, 2D and tilted 3D phases on WebGPU and forced WebGL2 and compare against baselines within tolerance
Verify holes are empty and the continent-sized polygon follows the globe curvature without cutting through it
Verify triangulation runs in a worker and handles self-touching and degenerate input without crashing

features.description: Extruded polygons render as solid shaded volumes with configurable height and base height, with correct depth ordering and no z-fighting against the ground.
steps: Open `?scenario=data-extrusions` with adjacent and overlapping extruded polygons of different heights on flat and sloped terrain
Orbit the tilted view and record every frame on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Verify walls and roofs are shaded, faces occlude correctly, and frame differencing shows no z-fighting shimmer at the ground or between touching walls
Verify extrusion heights match the configured values within 1% when measured through picking

features.description: Circles and ellipses are defined by a center, radii in meters and rotation, and keep their true ground shape on the ellipsoid at any latitude.
steps: Open `?scenario=data-circles` with circles and ellipses at the equator, at 60° latitude and near a pole
Verify sampled outline points lie at the configured geodesic distance from the center within 0.1% using the geodesic utilities
Capture screenshots in the globe, 2D and tilted 3D phases on WebGPU and forced WebGL2 and compare against baselines within tolerance

features.description: Label primitives display text attached to a coordinate with configurable font, size, color, halo, anchor and offset.
steps: Open `?scenario=data-labels` with labels using several fonts, sizes, colors, halos, anchors and offsets
Capture screenshots on WebGPU and forced WebGL2 and compare against baselines within tolerance
Verify text with accented Latin, Greek and Cyrillic characters renders with the correct glyphs, and CJK text renders through a fallback font
Verify the label anchor stays on its coordinate within 1 pixel while panning and zooming

features.description: Labels use signed distance field glyphs, so text stays crisp at any size, zoom and pixel density.
steps: Render the same labels at sizes from 8 to 64 px at device pixel ratio 1, 2 and 3
Measure edge sharpness in screenshots and verify it meets the documented threshold at every size on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Zoom continuously while recording frames and verify text shows no blur steps or shimmer by frame differencing
Verify glyphs are generated or loaded off the main thread and cached in an atlas

features.description: Labels avoid overlapping through collision detection and decluttering, keeping higher-priority labels when space is short.
steps: Open a scenario with 10,000 labels of mixed priorities in a dense area
Capture a screenshot and verify through the debug collision boxes that no two visible labels overlap
Verify that whenever two labels collide, the one with higher priority is the one shown
Zoom in and verify hidden labels appear as space frees up, with collision work staying within the per-frame budget

features.description: Labels do not flicker, jitter or pop while the camera pans, zooms, rotates or tilts; labels entering or leaving collision fade in and out.
steps: Run scripted pan, zoom, rotate and tilt paths over a dense labeled area and record every frame on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Run temporal glitch detection and verify no label toggles visibility more than once within the fade window and none jumps more than 1 pixel between frames beyond camera motion
Verify visibility changes are fades of the documented duration, not single-frame pops

features.description: glTF 2.0 models load and render at a coordinate with heading, pitch, roll and scale, including PBR materials, textures, Draco-compressed geometry and KTX2 textures.
steps: Load a set of Khronos glTF 2.0 sample models (.glb and .gltf with external resources, Draco and KTX2 variants) through the glTF loader
Run the glTF adapter conformance suite against the Khronos sample models and assert it passes
Place them at several coordinates with different heading, pitch, roll and scale and capture screenshots on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Compare against reference renderings within tolerance and verify orientation relative to local east-north-up axes
Feed truncated and corrupted glTF files and verify the loader rejects them with an error event and no crash or blank view
Verify decoding runs in workers and models are positioned without jitter at street level

features.description: Primitives can be placed at an absolute altitude above the WGS84 ellipsoid, and their screen position is correct in every phase.
steps: Place points, markers, lines and models at 0 m, 1,000 m and 10,000 m absolute altitude
Verify their screen positions match the projection of their ellipsoidal coordinates within 1 pixel in the globe, 2D and tilted 3D phases
Verify on the flat plane that altitude is scaled consistently with the terrain relief scaling, so objects stay at the same height relative to the terrain

features.description: Markers and models clamped to the ground sit on the terrain surface and are re-adjusted smoothly when finer terrain detail loads.
steps: Place ground-clamped markers and models across a mountainous area and zoom from the globe to street level
After each terrain refinement, verify each object's base height equals the terrain height under it within the documented tolerance
Record every frame and verify by frame differencing that re-adjustment never causes a visible jump
Verify objects are never visibly floating above or sunk into the terrain at any recorded frame

features.description: Polylines draped on terrain follow the relief at every terrain level, never floating above it or cutting into it.
steps: Open `?scenario=draped-lines` with lines across ridges and valleys in the Alps
Zoom from the globe to street level and orbit in the tilted view on WebGPU and forced WebGL2, recording every frame
Verify every frame shows each line fully visible on the terrain with no gaps where it would be hidden and no segment detached from the surface
Verify behavior stays correct during terrain level changes and geomorphing

features.description: Polygons draped on terrain follow the relief at every terrain level, never floating above it or cutting into it.
steps: Open `?scenario=draped-polygons` with filled and outlined polygons over steep terrain
Zoom from the globe to street level and orbit in the tilted view on WebGPU and forced WebGL2, recording every frame
Verify the fill covers exactly the polygon area on the terrain with no gaps or terrain poking through, and outlines stay on the surface
Verify behavior stays correct during terrain level changes and geomorphing

features.description: Data layers stay attached to their geographic positions through the globe-to-flat morph and the tilt into 3D, with no sliding, jump or layer lag behind the map.
steps: Load points, lines, polygons, labels and models over a city and run a continuous zoom from the globe to an oblique street view
Record every frame and verify each primitive's screen position matches the morphed map position under it within 1 pixel
Verify there is no frame where layers and map are out of sync on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: Data primitives show no vertex jitter at street level on either backend.
steps: Place points, lines, polygons, labels and models at street level in several cities far from the origin, including high longitudes and latitudes
Zoom to about 1 m above the ground and record frames while making sub-meter camera moves
Verify by frame analysis that no primitive vertex moves relative to the ground by more than 1 pixel beyond camera motion on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: Lines, polygons, circles and labels crossing the antimeridian or near the poles render correctly in every phase.
steps: Load features crossing the antimeridian and features around both poles
Capture screenshots in the globe, 2D and tilted 3D phases on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Verify no feature wraps the wrong way around the world, shows a gap at ±180° or degenerates near a pole

features.description: Data-driven styles derive color, size, width, opacity, icon and text from feature properties.
steps: Load a dataset with numeric and categorical properties and style it with property-driven expressions for color, size, width, opacity, icon and text
Capture screenshots and verify each feature's style matches its properties
Change a feature property through a live update and verify its style updates in the next frame without rebuilding the layer
Feed malformed style expressions and verify they are rejected at the API boundary with a clear error

features.description: Zoom-dependent styles change size, width, opacity and visibility with zoom, interpolating continuously with no visible steps unless a step is explicitly defined.
steps: Style a layer with zoom-interpolated size, width and opacity and a zoom-stepped visibility
Zoom continuously while recording frames
Verify interpolated properties change smoothly by frame differencing and the stepped property switches exactly at its stop

features.description: GeoJSON, KML, GPX and Mapbox Vector Tile data load into data layers from a URL, a File or an in-memory object, parsed off the main thread.
steps: Load fixture files of each format from a URL, from a File object and from an in-memory object
Verify the rendered features match the fixture geometry and properties
Verify parsing runs in a worker and the main thread has no long task above 50 ms while loading a 50 MB GeoJSON file
Load corrupted files of each format and verify an error event with no crash or blank view

features.description: Features streamed incrementally from an application API appear progressively without rebuilding the layer or blocking the main thread.
steps: Stream 100,000 features from a mock application API in chunks of 1,000 over 30 seconds
Verify each chunk becomes visible within one frame of being added
Verify frame time stays within the target throughout and no full layer rebuild occurs (instrumentation counters)

features.description: Point and marker layers cluster nearby features into cluster symbols with counts, splitting and merging smoothly as the zoom changes.
steps: Load 100,000 points with clustering enabled and zoom from the globe to street level
Verify cluster counts always sum to the number of features in view
Record every frame and verify clusters split and merge with animated transitions, without pops or flicker, by frame differencing
Verify clustering is computed in a worker and clicking a cluster zooms to its extent

features.description: Marker layers apply level of detail: distant or dense markers draw as simplified symbols and switch smoothly to full markers when close.
steps: Load 100,000 markers and zoom from a continental view to street level
Verify through the debug overlay that far or dense markers use the simplified representation and near ones the full marker
Verify the switch is a cross-fade with no pop by frame differencing and draw calls stay within the documented budget

features.description: Layers with hundreds of thousands of points load off the main thread and stay interactive within the memory budget.
steps: Load 500,000 points with clustering from a fixture
Verify the main thread has no long task above 50 ms during loading
Pan and zoom for 60 seconds and verify the engine stays responsive, RAM and GPU memory stay within budget, and no crash occurs

features.description: Changing a single feature's position updates only that feature's GPU data, without rebuilding the layer.
steps: Load a 100,000-point layer and move one feature every frame
Verify the feature appears at its new position in the next frame
Verify through instrumentation that only the changed range is uploaded and the per-frame update cost stays within budget

features.description: Changing a single feature's style or visibility updates it in the next frame without rebuilding the layer.
steps: Load a 100,000-point layer and toggle visibility and change color and size of individual features
Verify each change is visible in the next frame
Verify through instrumentation that only the changed ranges are uploaded

features.description: A live sensor-style feed updating 10,000 features per second on a 100,000-feature layer keeps the target frame rate.
steps: Run `?scenario=live-feed` with a 100,000-feature layer receiving 10,000 position and style updates per second
Record frame times for 60 seconds while panning and zooming
Verify p95 frame time is at most 16.7 ms on the reference desktop and the per-frame JavaScript heap allocation stays at zero in the render loop

features.description: Hovering a feature emits hover enter and leave events carrying the feature, its layer and the geographic coordinates, and applies an optional hover style.
steps: Move the mouse across features of every primitive type in a scripted path
Verify enter and leave events fire once each in the right order with the feature, layer and coordinates
Verify the hover style is applied and removed in the next frame
Verify hover picking on a 100,000-point layer stays within the per-frame budget

features.description: Clicking or tapping a feature emits a click event carrying the feature, its layer, the geographic coordinates and the elevation of the picked point.
steps: Click features of every primitive type with the mouse and tap them with touch emulation
Verify the event carries the correct feature, layer, longitude, latitude and elevation
Click overlapping features and verify the topmost one is reported
Manually verify tapping on the reference tablet

features.description: Selected features show a selection highlight that stays correct while the camera moves and the feature updates.
steps: Select features of every primitive type by click and through the API
Verify the highlight appears in the next frame and is removed on deselection
Move the camera and live-update the selected feature and verify the highlight follows it

features.description: Features marked draggable can be dragged with mouse or touch, emitting drag start, move and end events with the new coordinates.
steps: Mark points, markers and models as draggable and drag them with the mouse and with touch emulation
Verify drag start, move and end events with correct coordinates, and that the map does not pan while dragging a feature
Verify dragged ground-clamped features stay on the terrain
Verify features are not draggable unless enabled

features.description: Picking on bare terrain returns the geographic coordinates and elevation of the point under the cursor.
steps: Click bare terrain at known locations at several zoom levels in the globe, 2D and tilted 3D phases
Verify coordinates match the expected location within the size of one screen pixel on the ground
Verify the elevation matches the best available terrain height within the documented tolerance on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: Picking returns the correct feature in every phase and on both backends, including at street level and during camera motion.
steps: Run an automated pick test that clicks 1,000 known feature positions in the globe, 2D and tilted 3D phases on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Verify every pick returns the expected feature, including small features at street level
Repeat during a running flight and verify picks match what is displayed in that frame

features.description: Removing a data layer frees its GPU buffers, textures and worker resources, with no growth over repeated add and remove cycles.
steps: Add and remove a layer with every primitive type 100 times
Verify GPU and RAM memory return to their baseline within tolerance after each cycle
Verify no listeners, workers or timers remain from removed layers

features.description: The data layers guide explains primitives, placement, styling, clustering, labels, picking, events and live updates with runnable examples.
steps: Open the data layers guide in the documentation site
Verify every topic listed is covered with a runnable example
Run every example from the guide and verify it works as described

features.description: Fitting to objects (features, positions and models, including their heights) frames all of them with the requested padding.
steps: Add point, line, polygon and elevated features to the playground and call fit-to-objects with padding
Project every object's extent (including height) to the screen after the animation
Assert all are inside the padded viewport and the view is not wider than needed (one edge within 2 px of the padding)

features.description: A consumer can implement a custom layer type through the public layer plug-in interface, outside the engine packages, and it renders, picks and receives frame and camera events like the built-in layers.
steps: Create a test package outside packages/ that implements a custom layer type against the public layer interface only
Type-check it in strict mode with no `any`
Add it in the playground and capture screenshots on WebGPU and forced WebGL2, asserting it renders at its expected coordinates
Assert it receives frame and camera events and that picking returns its features

features.description: Milestone 10 acceptance: 100,000 points with clustering stay at the target frame rate, and draped shapes follow terrain at every level.
steps: Run `?scenario=points-100k` with 100,000 clustered points through scripted pan, zoom, rotate and flight paths on the reference desktop
Verify p95 frame time is at most 16.7 ms on the reference desktop and at least 30 fps on the reference tablet
Run the draped lines and polygons scenarios from the globe to street level on WebGPU and forced WebGL2 and verify shapes follow the terrain in every recorded frame
Confirm no known bug remains open for this milestone
A fresh-context reviewer checks the milestone against PLAN.md and its acceptance criteria and reports no correctness or requirement gaps

features.description: The atmosphere and lighting research survey is written in docs/research/: approaches, trade-offs, known failure modes from issue trackers, tests and benchmarks studied, and the chosen approach with reasons.
steps: Open the atmosphere and lighting survey in docs/research/
Verify it studies at least CesiumJS, three.js, Babylon.js, OpenGlobus, osgEarth and Filament, and the O'Neil and Bruneton-Neyret papers
Verify it lists known failure modes with issue references (for example banding, precision artifacts near the horizon, discontinuities at altitude changes, cost on tablets)
Verify it states the chosen approach, why, and how it will be tested

features.description: A sky renders whenever the globe or the horizon is visible, instead of a flat background color.
steps: Capture screenshots of the globe from orbit and of tilted views showing the horizon at several altitudes
Verify the background above the horizon is sky (no flat clear color, no black area adjacent to the horizon in tilted views) on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Compare against baselines within tolerance

features.description: An atmosphere glow surrounds the globe limb and changes smoothly with altitude, with no banding.
steps: Fly from orbit to the ground while recording every frame on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Verify by frame differencing that atmosphere brightness and color change continuously with no jumps
Verify gradients show no visible 8-bit banding (dithering or equivalent), measured on screenshots

features.description: Sky, atmosphere and haze transition continuously through the globe-to-flat morph and the tilt into the 3D view, with no jump at phase boundaries.
steps: Run a continuous zoom from the globe to an oblique street view recording every frame
Run temporal glitch detection on the sky and atmosphere regions and verify no frame-to-frame jump above threshold at any phase boundary
Repeat on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: Atmospheric haze or fog fades distant terrain and imagery in tilted views, hiding low-detail tiles near the horizon.
steps: Open a tilted view at the maximum tilt over terrain with the horizon visible
Verify distant terrain and imagery blend into the haze color with distance
Verify tile-boundary contrast near the horizon stays below the seam detector threshold, so low-detail tiles are not distinguishable from their neighbors
Repeat on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: Fog reduces tile loads near the horizon: fully fogged areas are not requested at fine levels.
steps: Run the same tilted flight scenario with fog enabled and disabled and count tile requests and GPU memory
Verify the fog-enabled run requests at least 25% fewer tiles over the scenario (the measured reduction is recorded in the ADR) with no visible difference in the fogged region
Verify no black or empty pixels appear near the horizon in either run

features.description: Optional sun lighting by date and time shades the globe and terrain with the day-night terminator at the astronomically correct position.
steps: Enable sun lighting and set several dates and times, including solstices and equinoxes
Verify the computed sun direction matches a reference solar ephemeris within 0.1°
Capture screenshots and verify the terminator position and terrain shading direction match the sun direction on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Verify lighting is off unless enabled and changing the time updates the view without a full reload

features.description: Anti-aliasing suited to each backend removes jagged edges on terrain silhouettes, lines and extruded shapes without shimmer in motion.
steps: Capture screenshots of terrain silhouettes, thin lines and extruded buildings on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Measure edge aliasing and verify it is below the documented threshold on both backends
Pan slowly while recording frames and verify no edge shimmer by temporal glitch detection
Verify the anti-aliasing cost stays within the per-frame GPU budget

features.description: Anisotropic filtering keeps imagery sharp in tilted views up to the maximum tilt, using the highest level the device supports.
steps: Open a tilted view at the maximum tilt over detailed imagery
Measure imagery sharpness in the distance with anisotropic filtering enabled and disabled and verify the documented improvement
Verify the anisotropy level equals the device maximum reported by capability detection, unless the quality preset lowers it
Repeat on WebGPU and forced WebGL2

features.description: Quality presets low, medium, high and ultra control level of detail, resolution scale and effects, and can be switched at runtime without a visible glitch.
steps: Switch between every preset at runtime while the camera moves
Verify each preset applies its documented level of detail, resolution scale and effect settings
Record every frame and verify switching never shows black areas, flicker or a frozen frame
Verify frame time decreases from ultra to low on the reference desktop

features.description: On startup the engine picks a sensible quality preset from capability detection (backend, GPU limits, memory hints), and applications can override it.
steps: Start the playground with emulated low-end and high-end capability profiles and verify the documented preset is chosen for each
Start on the reference desktop and reference tablet and verify the chosen presets
Pass an explicit preset in the configuration and verify it overrides detection

features.description: Adaptive quality watches frame time and lowers detail or resolution automatically when the frame rate drops below the target.
steps: Inject an artificial GPU load in the playground so frame time exceeds the target
Verify adaptive quality lowers detail or resolution within the documented reaction time and frame time returns within the target
Record frames and verify the reduction causes no visible pop or flicker

features.description: Adaptive quality raises detail back once performance is stable, with hysteresis so quality never oscillates.
steps: Remove the injected load after adaptive quality has lowered quality
Verify quality rises back step by step to the preset level once frame time has been stable for the documented interval
Run a load that hovers around the threshold for 5 minutes and verify quality changes no more often than the documented minimum interval

features.description: Milestone 11 acceptance: adaptive quality holds the target frame rate on the reference tablet.
steps: Run the scripted zoom, pan, rotation, tilt and flight scenarios on the reference tablet with adaptive quality enabled and every effect on
Verify at least 30 fps (p95 frame time at most 33.3 ms) throughout, aiming for 60 fps
Verify zero black pixels and no popping in the recorded frames
Confirm no known bug remains open for this milestone
A fresh-context reviewer checks the milestone against PLAN.md and its acceptance criteria and reports no correctness or requirement gaps

features.description: Coordinates transform between reference systems (for example WGS84, Web Mercator, UTM zones 32N and 33N, ETRS89) through a permissively licensed projection library, and custom systems can be defined.
steps: Transform reference points between the listed systems and verify results match EPSG reference values within 1 mm
Run property-based round-trip tests for every built-in transform
Define a custom reference system from a projection definition string and verify a transform through it
Verify the projection library's license passes the license audit

features.description: Public functions format coordinates as decimal degrees, degrees-minutes-seconds and UTM with configurable precision, shared by the readout and the go-to search.
steps: Format reference coordinates in each format and precision and verify against expected strings, including hemispheres, zone letters and rounding at 60 seconds
Run property-based tests verifying that parsing each formatted string returns the original coordinate within the format's precision
Verify the readout control and the search box use these functions

features.description: The coordinates readout control shows the coordinates and terrain elevation under the pointer, updated live, in the selected format, with mouse, touch and keyboard.
steps: Move the mouse over known locations and verify coordinates and elevation match expected values within the documented tolerance
With touch emulation, tap and long-press and verify the readout shows the touched point; manually verify on the reference tablet
Using only the keyboard, switch format between decimal degrees, DMS and UTM and verify the readout reports the view center while navigating by keyboard
Verify the readout updates within one frame and costs no more than its per-frame budget

features.description: The drawing tool draws points, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard.
steps: Activate point drawing and place points with mouse clicks, with touch taps and with the keyboard (move cursor, confirm)
Verify drawn points appear at the expected coordinates, ground-clamped, and are returned through the API and events
Verify placing a point never pans or zooms the map by accident

features.description: The drawing tool draws lines, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard, with lines draped on terrain.
steps: Draw a multi-vertex line with mouse clicks, with touch taps and with the keyboard, finishing with double-click, double-tap and Enter respectively
Verify the line preview follows the pointer while drawing and the final line drapes on the terrain
Verify the resulting geometry is returned through the API and events with the expected coordinates

features.description: The drawing tool draws polygons, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard, with polygons draped on terrain.
steps: Draw polygons with mouse, touch and keyboard, closing on the first vertex or with the finish action
Verify the preview, the closed draped polygon and the geometry returned through the API and events
Verify self-intersecting input is reported to the application through a validation event

features.description: Drawn points, lines and polygons can be edited: move vertices, insert and delete vertices, move whole shapes, with mouse, touch and keyboard.
steps: Edit each shape type by dragging vertices, inserting a vertex on an edge midpoint, deleting a vertex and moving the whole shape, with the mouse
Repeat with touch emulation and with the keyboard only; manually verify on the reference tablet
Verify change events carry the updated geometry after each edit and shapes stay draped on terrain

features.description: Measurement tools built on the drawing tools measure geodesic distance, path length, area and bearing with live readouts and automatic unit scaling.
steps: Measure a known distance, a multi-segment path and a known polygon area with mouse, touch and keyboard
Verify the live readout values match the geodesic utilities within display precision and update while drawing and editing
Verify units scale automatically (meters to kilometers, square meters to square kilometers) and labels are translated in English and Italian

features.description: The scale bar is referred to the view center, stays accurate in tilted views, and updates live while navigating.
steps: Show the scale bar at several zoom levels in the globe, 2D and tilted 3D phases
Verify the represented length matches the geodesic ground distance across the bar's screen length at the view center within 1%
Pan, zoom and tilt and verify the bar updates within one frame without flicker
Verify the control is readable with the keyboard focus and by screen readers (accessible text with the current scale)

features.description: Geolocation shows the user's position with its accuracy and flies to it, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard, handling denied or unavailable permission.
steps: Grant emulated geolocation in Playwright and activate the control with mouse, touch and keyboard
Verify the position marker and accuracy circle appear at the emulated position and the camera flies there honoring the view-mode rules
Move the emulated position and verify the marker follows
Deny permission and verify a translated message appears and the engine keeps working

features.description: The camera state (position, zoom, heading, tilt and view mode, chosen and applied) serializes to and from a URL and JSON exactly.
steps: Navigate to several views in each view mode and serialize them to a URL and to JSON
Open each URL in a new page and load each JSON and verify the restored camera equals the original within floating-point tolerance and the screenshots match
Run property-based round-trip tests on random camera states
Feed malformed and out-of-range URLs and JSON and verify they are rejected or clamped with no crash

features.description: Saved views and bookmarks can be created, listed, opened and removed through the API and the UI.
steps: Save several views through the API and through the UI with mouse, touch and keyboard
Verify they are listed with names and can be opened, flying to the saved camera
Remove a bookmark and verify it disappears
Export and re-import the bookmarks as JSON and verify they are identical

features.description: A screenshot of the current view exports at a chosen resolution, larger than the canvas if requested, complete with all tiles and the required attribution.
steps: Export screenshots at the canvas size, at 2x and at 4096x4096 on WebGPU and forced WebGL2
Verify each image has the requested size, contains zero black or empty pixels and matches the view content
Verify required attributions and logos are included in the image
Verify the live view keeps rendering without stutter during export
Export a view containing Google content and assert the export follows the Google terms ADR and always includes the Google logo and attributions

features.description: An optional overview minimap shows the current view footprint, updated live, within its performance budget.
steps: Enable the minimap and navigate in the globe, 2D and tilted 3D phases
Verify the footprint matches the main view's visible area, including the trapezoid of tilted views
Verify the minimap adds no more than its documented per-frame cost and is absent unless enabled

features.description: The core runs headless; the optional ui package adds ready-made controls that applications can add, remove, extend or replace individually.
steps: Run the engine without the ui package and verify no UI code is loaded (bundle analysis)
Add controls individually and remove them and verify each mounts and unmounts cleanly
Replace one built-in control with a custom control built on the public control API and extend another, and verify both work

features.description: The zoom +/- control zooms in and out smoothly, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard.
steps: Click the + and - buttons, tap them with touch emulation and activate them with the keyboard
Verify each action triggers an animated zoom step and repeated presses chain without jumps
Verify buttons are disabled at the minimum and maximum zoom
Manually verify on the reference tablet

features.description: The compass control shows the heading, resets north on click and rotates on drag, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard, including one-step orientation to N, E, S or W.
steps: Rotate the map and verify the compass needle shows the heading every frame
Click and tap the compass and verify an animated reset to north; drag it with mouse and touch and verify the map rotates
Using only the keyboard, reset north, rotate and orient to N, E, S and W
Manually verify on the reference tablet

features.description: The 2D / 3D / Auto toggle sets tilt to 0°, to the default tilt or back to the zoom-driven curves, with a visible Back to Auto control next to it, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard.
steps: Activate 2D, 3D and Auto with the mouse, touch emulation and the keyboard
Verify 2D sets tilt to 0°, 3D sets the default tilt and Auto restores the zoom-driven curves, each with a smooth transition
Verify the control shows the current mode, including after a manual tilt
Manually verify on the reference tablet

features.description: The tilt control sets and shows the chosen tilt, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard.
steps: Change tilt by dragging the control with the mouse and touch emulation and with the keyboard arrows
Verify the tilt changes smoothly and becomes the chosen tilt that persists across zoom
Verify the control shows the applied tilt and indicates when it is temporarily clamped
Manually verify on the reference tablet

features.description: The reset-to-globe and home-view controls fly to the whole globe and to the project home view, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard.
steps: Activate reset to globe and home with the mouse, touch emulation and the keyboard
Verify each triggers a flight to the expected view honoring the view-mode rules and reduced motion
Verify any user input during the flight interrupts it smoothly
Manually verify on the reference tablet

features.description: The attribution control shows credits for the sources currently visible, updated live, and is never hidden or covered by other controls.
steps: Pan between areas covered by different sources and verify the credits update within one frame of the visible sources changing
At desktop, tablet and phone viewport sizes with every control enabled, verify by layout bounding boxes that no control overlaps the attribution or a required provider logo
Verify a collapsed attribution on small screens still shows required logos and can be expanded with mouse, touch and keyboard
Verify attribution links are keyboard-focusable and announced by screen readers

features.description: The layer switcher lists layers and lets users choose the base layer and toggle overlay visibility, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard.
steps: Open the layer switcher with mouse, touch emulation and the keyboard
Switch base layers and toggle overlays and verify the map updates without black areas or flicker
Verify the list reflects layers added and removed through the API at runtime
Manually verify on the reference tablet

features.description: The search box uses the pluggable geocoder (no default provider) and also accepts typed coordinates, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard.
steps: Verify the search box offers only coordinate input when no geocoder is configured
Configure a mock geocoder, type a query and verify results are listed, navigable with arrow keys and selectable with Enter, click or tap
Verify selecting a result flies to it, and typed decimal degrees, DMS and UTM coordinates fly to the right place
Verify a failing or slow geocoder shows a translated message without blocking the map

features.description: The fullscreen control enters and exits fullscreen, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard, and is hidden where fullscreen is unsupported.
steps: Activate the control with mouse, touch emulation and the keyboard and verify the map container enters and exits fullscreen
Verify the canvas resizes without stretching, black areas or a frozen frame
Emulate a browser without the Fullscreen API and verify the control is hidden
Manually verify on the reference tablet

features.description: The debug panel toggle shows and hides the debug overlay and performance HUD, operable with mouse, touch and keyboard.
steps: Toggle the debug panel with mouse, touch emulation and the keyboard
Verify the debug overlay and performance HUD appear and disappear
Verify the toggle is absent unless enabled in the configuration

features.description: Every control is themed through documented CSS variables, so applications can restyle every control without overriding internal selectors.
steps: Apply a test theme that changes every documented CSS variable
Capture screenshots of every control and verify each visual property changed as expected
Run an automated check that the ui package stylesheets contain no hard-coded colors, fonts or sizes outside the variable defaults

features.description: Light and dark themes are included and can be switched at runtime.
steps: Switch between light and dark themes at runtime
Capture screenshots of every control in both themes and compare against baselines within tolerance
Verify the switch applies to every control without reload

features.description: English and Italian translations are included for every UI string and can be switched at runtime.
steps: Switch the language between English and Italian at runtime and verify every control's text, tooltips and ARIA labels change
Run an automated check that both languages define every translation key
Verify numbers and units are formatted according to the selected locale

features.description: Translations are pluggable: an application can register a new language or override strings without changing the ui package.
steps: Register a third test language from the application
Verify every control shows the new strings and missing keys fall back to English
Override a single English string and verify only that string changes

features.description: Every control is reachable and operable with the keyboard alone, in a logical focus order with a visible focus indicator.
steps: Tab through all controls in the playground and verify a logical focus order with no keyboard trap
Verify every focused control shows a visible focus indicator in light and dark themes
Operate every control with Enter, Space, arrows and Escape as documented

features.description: Every control has correct ARIA roles, names and states, and the UI passes an automated accessibility audit with zero violations.
steps: Run an automated accessibility audit (for example axe-core) on the playground with every control enabled, in both languages and both themes
Verify zero violations
Verify state changes (mode toggle, fullscreen, layer visibility) update ARIA states

features.description: All controls meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast in both light and dark themes.
steps: Run automated contrast checks on every control's text, icons and focus indicators in both themes
Verify every ratio meets WCAG 2.1 AA
Verify icons over the map keep sufficient contrast over light and dark imagery (backing shape or outline)

features.description: With the system reduced-motion setting, UI animations are removed and actions that trigger flights use quick fades.
steps: Emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce in Playwright
Activate every control that animates and verify no UI animation plays and camera flights become quick fades
Verify behavior returns to normal when the setting is off

features.description: Controls lay out without overlapping each other or the attribution on desktop and tablet viewport sizes in both orientations, with touch targets of at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels; on phone sizes (best effort) the attribution and required logos stay visible.
steps: Render the playground with every control enabled at desktop and tablet viewport sizes in portrait and landscape
Verify by bounding boxes that no two controls overlap and none covers the attribution
Verify every interactive element on touch devices has a target of at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels
At phone viewport sizes in both orientations, verify the attribution and every required logo stay fully visible and uncovered

features.description: Milestone 12 acceptance: every control works with mouse, touch and keyboard alone.
steps: Run the automated control suite three times, once using only the mouse, once only touch emulation and once only the keyboard, exercising every ready-made control and GIS tool
Verify every action succeeds in each run, in English and Italian, in light and dark themes
Manually exercise every control on the reference tablet with touch alone and on the reference desktop with keyboard alone
Confirm no known bug remains open for this milestone
A fresh-context reviewer checks the milestone against PLAN.md and its acceptance criteria and reports no correctness or requirement gaps

features.description: A written research survey on vector tiles, building extrusion and 3D Tiles streaming exists in docs/research/ before the subsystem is built, and the chosen approach is justified.
steps: Open the vector tiles, buildings and 3D Tiles survey in docs/research/

Check it studies MapLibre GL JS, MapLibre Native, Tangram, OpenLayers, deck.gl, CesiumJS, 3DTilesRendererJS, iTowns and loaders.gl for MVT decoding and tessellation, style evaluation, symbol placement, extrusion rendering, 3D Tiles traversal, refinement and caching

Check it lists the known bugs and glitches found in their issue trackers (vector seams at tile edges, label flicker, extrusion z-fighting, 3D Tiles holes and memory growth) and how their tests and benchmarks catch them
Check it records the approaches found, their trade-offs and failure modes, the chosen approach and why, with a linked ADR
Confirm no restrictively licensed source-available project (for example Mapbox GL JS v2+) was studied and no code was copied

features.description: Mapbox Vector Tiles render as fills, lines and points on the flat 2D map, crisp at every fractional zoom and without seams at tile edges.
steps: Open the playground with `?scenario=mvt-flat` (fixture MVT tileset and a reference style) on `?backend=webgpu` and `?backend=webgl2`
Capture screenshots at zoom 4, 8.5, 12, 14.25 and 16 and compare them with reviewed baselines within the visual-test tolerance
Record every frame of a continuous zoom from 10 to 16 and assert line widths and fills change continuously, with no stepping at integer zoom levels
Sample pixels along tile boundaries and assert no gaps, double-drawn lines or color discontinuities at tile edges

features.description: Vector tiles render on the globe and through the globe-to-flat morph with no gaps, seams or jumps, and look the same in the globe, 2D and 3D phases.
steps: Open `?scenario=mvt-globe-zoom` and record every frame of a zoom from the whole globe to city level on both backends
Assert zero background or black pixels inside the globe after the base has loaded, including at the antimeridian and the polar caps
Assert by frame differencing that vector features do not jump or slide during the morph
Capture the same area in the globe, 2D and 3D phases and assert colors, line widths and feature presence match within tolerance

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: Beyond a vector source's maximum zoom the deepest tiles are overzoomed, and a parent vector tile stays visible until its children are ready, so vector content never disappears.
steps: Load a fixture vector tileset with maxzoom 14 and zoom to 19; assert features are still drawn crisply and no tile above zoom 14 is requested (request log)
Throttle the network to a slow profile and record frames while zooming quickly between 10 and 16
Assert no frame shows an empty area where vector content exists at a coarser level
Assert out-of-coverage vector tiles are never requested

features.description: MVT decoding, geometry tessellation and label layout preparation run in workers, keeping main-thread time per frame within budget during fast navigation over dense vector data.
steps: Open `?scenario=mvt-city` (dense city vector tiles) and record a performance trace during a fast pan and zoom
Assert decoding and tessellation performance marks appear only on worker threads
Assert main-thread CPU time per frame stays within the per-frame budget documented in docs/plan
Assert no long task (over 50 ms) occurs on the main thread while tiles load

features.description: An existing MapLibre Style Specification style (sources, sprite, glyphs, layers) loads without edits and renders the map as intended.
steps: Load an openly licensed MapLibre style (for example one built for the OpenMapTiles schema) pointed at the self-hosted fixture tiles, without changing the style JSON
Assert the style validates with no errors and all its layers are created
Capture screenshots of canonical views and compare them with reviewed reference images within the documented tolerance
Repeat on both backends

features.description: Every layer type of the pinned MapLibre Style Specification version renders: background, fill, line, symbol, circle, fill-extrusion, raster, hillshade and heatmap.
steps: Record the supported specification version in an ADR
Open one playground fixture per layer type and capture screenshots on both backends
Compare each screenshot with its reviewed baseline within tolerance
Assert line properties (width, dasharray, cap, join, gradient) and fill properties (pattern, outline, opacity) render as specified

features.description: Style expressions, filters, zoom functions and feature-state follow the MapLibre Style Specification semantics, including data-driven and zoom-dependent styling.
steps: Run unit tests covering every expression operator family (lookup, decision, ramps and interpolation, math, string, color, type conversion, zoom, feature-state) against the specification's documented semantics
Assert legacy filter syntax and current expression filters select the same features
Record frames during a continuous zoom and assert interpolated paint properties change smoothly
Set feature-state on a feature at runtime and assert its style changes on the next frame

features.description: Style layer order, minzoom, maxzoom and visibility are honored, and layers enter or leave their zoom range with a cross-fade instead of popping.
steps: Load a fixture style with layers limited to zoom ranges and overlapping fills in a defined order
Assert the draw order matches the style layer order in screenshots
Record frames while zooming across each minzoom and maxzoom and assert frame differences show a fade, not a single-frame pop
Toggle visibility at runtime and assert the layer hides and shows without reloading tiles

features.description: Style sprites (1x and 2x) and glyph ranges load from the style's URLs, and icons and signed-distance-field text render crisply at every size and pixel density.
