steps: Load a style with sprite and glyphs URLs at device pixel ratio 1 and 2
Assert the 2x sprite is used at ratio 2 and icons are not blurry (edge-sharpness check against baseline)
Assert text from 10 to 32 px is crisp and glyph ranges are requested only for characters in use
Render labels with Latin, Cyrillic, Greek and CJK characters and assert each renders or falls back to a configured font without missing boxes

features.description: Vector-tile symbol layers place point labels and labels along lines with collision detection and priorities, never duplicated across tile boundaries and without flicker during motion.
steps: Open `?scenario=mvt-labels` and read placed label boxes through the debug API
Assert no two placed labels overlap and higher-priority labels win collisions
Assert road labels follow curved lines and are not duplicated where a road crosses a tile boundary
Record frames during slow pan, zoom, rotate and tilt and assert labels fade in and out with no flicker (frame differencing)

features.description: Paint and layout properties, filters and layers of a vector style can be changed at runtime and the view updates without reloading tiles or showing a blank frame.
steps: Call the style API to change a paint property, a layout property and a filter, and to add and remove a layer
Assert paint changes appear on the next frame and layout changes within the documented time
Assert from the request log that no tile is downloaded again
Assert no recorded frame during the changes contains black or empty pixels

features.description: Invalid or partly unsupported styles are validated on load: problems are reported with the offending path, valid layers still render, and malformed styles never crash or blank the view.
steps: Load a style containing an unknown property, a wrongly typed value and a layer referencing a missing source
Assert each problem is reported through the engine log and error event with its JSON path
Assert the valid layers render normally
Fuzz style JSON with random mutations in Vitest and assert no exception escapes the engine and the view is never blank

features.description: In the 3D view, vector-tile fills and lines are draped on terrain and follow the relief without floating above it or cutting into it, at every terrain level.
steps: Open `?scenario=mvt-terrain` over a mountain fixture with terrain enabled and tilt to 60 degrees
Capture screenshots on both backends and compare with baselines
Compare the depth of road pixels with the terrain surface depth and assert they lie on the surface within tolerance
Zoom across several terrain levels and assert lines stay on the surface with no shimmer (frame differencing)

features.description: OpenStreetMap roads from the self-hosted extract render with class-based styling from motorways to paths, correct bridge and tunnel layering, and road names.
steps: Load the Italy OpenStreetMap vector tiles built by the data pipeline and open central Milan
Capture screenshots at zoom 12, 15 and 17 and compare with reviewed baselines
Assert bridges draw above the roads they cross and tunnels draw below or dashed as styled
Assert road-name labels appear along the roads at street zoom

features.description: OpenStreetMap places (countries, regions, cities, towns, villages, neighborhoods) appear as labels ranked by importance and decluttered at every zoom, in the configured language with fallback.
steps: Zoom from the globe to street level over Italy and capture screenshots at each phase
Assert capitals and large cities are labeled before smaller places and no labels overlap
Switch the label language between English and Italian and assert names use name:en or name:it with a fallback to name
Assert place labels do not flicker during the zoom (frame differencing)

features.description: OpenStreetMap buildings are extruded to their real height using height, min_height and building:levels data, including building parts.
steps: Load a fixture of buildings with known height, min_height, building:levels and building:part tags
Read each extruded building's top and base height through the picking or debug API
Assert height matches the height tag, otherwise levels times the per-level height recorded in the ADR
Assert min_height produces raised parts and building parts replace their outline correctly
Compare a Milan view with extrusions against the reviewed baseline

features.description: Buildings without height data get deterministic sensible default heights by building type, documented in the engine.
steps: Load a fixture of buildings without height or level tags of several types (house, apartments, commercial, industrial, church, garage)
Assert each gets the default height from the documented table
Reload and pan so the buildings come from different tiles and assert the heights are identical
Check the defaults table is documented in the data layers guide

features.description: Extruded buildings render with shading, anti-aliased edges, no z-fighting with the ground or each other, and appear without popping as the camera zooms in.
steps: Record every frame of a zoom from city to street level over Milan on both backends
Assert no shimmer at building bases and coplanar roofs (temporal z-fighting analysis)
Assert buildings fade or grow in rather than pop (frame differencing below the popping threshold)
Assert walls facing different directions receive different shading in screenshots

features.description: Building heights on the flat map are scaled consistently with the projection's scale factor, while measurements of a building's height stay true on the ellipsoid.
steps: Place the camera over buildings of known height at latitudes 0, 45 and 60 degrees
Assert the rendered height relative to the rendered ground scale matches the projection scale factor at each latitude
Measure a building's height through the engine API and assert it equals the source height in meters

features.description: Hovering or clicking a vector-tile feature or building returns its properties and coordinates in the event and highlights it.
steps: Hover and click a road, a place label and an extruded building with Playwright
Assert hover and click events carry the feature's layer, properties and geographic coordinates
Assert the selection highlight appears on the picked feature in a screenshot
Repeat on both backends and with touch emulation

features.description: The 3D Tiles adapter loads OGC 3D Tiles 1.0 and 1.1 tilesets (external tilesets, b3dm, i3dm, pnts, cmpt and glTF content, implicit tiling, metadata, box/region/sphere volumes) and passes its conformance suite.
steps: Run the 3D Tiles conformance suite against fixture tilesets for every content type and bounding volume
Assert transforms, bounding volumes, geometric errors and metadata are parsed as specified
Fuzz tileset JSON and binary tile content and assert no crash, the tile is marked failed and its parent stays visible
Run the suite against public sample tilesets where their terms allow it

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: 3D Tiles stream by screen-space error from each tile's geometric error with REPLACE and ADD refinement, and a parent stays visible until all children replacing it are ready, so no holes appear.
steps: Open `?scenario=3dtiles-city` and record every frame while zooming in and out on both backends
Assert zero background pixels inside the tileset footprint after the root tile has loaded
Repeat with a slow network profile and assert still no holes
Check the debug overlay shows each tile's level and screen-space error

features.section: Tiles, level of detail and streaming
features.description: 3D Tiles requests go through the engine scheduler with priorities, per-host concurrency and cancellation during flights, and 3D Tiles memory stays within the GPU and RAM budgets with LRU eviction.
steps: flyTo across a large tileset and assert from the request log that requests for tiles no longer needed are cancelled
Assert screen-center tiles are requested before peripheral ones
Run 10 minutes of randomized navigation and assert GPU and RAM use stay within the configured budgets
Assert evicted tiles reload correctly when revisited

features.description: Draco, meshopt and KTX2/Basis compressed 3D Tiles content decodes in workers, with decoders loaded lazily from configurable URLs only when a tileset needs them.
steps: Load fixture tilesets using Draco, meshopt and KTX2 textures
Assert decoding marks appear only in workers and the main thread stays within its frame budget
Assert decoder files are requested only after a tileset that needs them is added
Serve decoders from a custom URL configured in the engine and assert they load from there

features.description: 3D Tiles render at street level without vertex jitter and stay aligned with imagery, terrain and data layers on the WGS84 ellipsoid.
steps: Place the camera 2 m above a tileset far from the origin and move it by sub-centimeter steps
Record frames and assert vertices do not jitter (frame differencing with a static scene)
Assert surveyed reference points in the tileset project onto the same pixels as markers placed at their WGS84 coordinates
Repeat on both backends

features.description: 3D Tiles look and behave the same in the globe, 2D map and 3D view phases and morph smoothly between them.
steps: Record every frame of a continuous zoom from the globe to an oblique view of a tileset
Assert by frame differencing that tileset geometry does not jump during the morph
Capture the same view in each phase and compare positions and colors within tolerance

features.description: Picking on 3D Tiles returns the picked tile feature, its batch or metadata properties and the picked coordinates and height.
steps: Click several features in a fixture tileset with per-feature batch tables and 1.1 metadata
Assert the click event carries the expected feature properties
Assert the reported coordinates and height match the fixture's known positions within tolerance

features.description: Where a 3D Tiles mesh overlaps the engine's terrain and imagery there is no z-fighting or show-through.
steps: Open a tileset covering ground that also has terrain and imagery
Record frames while orbiting at street level and assert no shimmer where the tileset meets the terrain (temporal z-fighting analysis)
Assert terrain does not show through the tileset surface in screenshots

features.description: Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles load through the Map Tiles API with the customer's own API key and session and render a city in the 3D view.
steps: Configure the Google adapter with an API key from the environment (never committed) and open Rome in the playground
Assert a session is created and photorealistic tiles stream and render
In CI, run the same flow against a mock Map Tiles server
Without a key, assert the playground shows a clear configuration message and the rest of the engine keeps working

features.description: Google 3D Tiles sessions are renewed when their token expires (about three hours) without a visible interruption or a reload.
steps: Run against a mock server whose session token expires after 60 seconds while navigating continuously
Assert a new session is requested before or at expiry and no tile request fails because of the expired token
Record frames across the renewal and assert no holes or blank frames
Manually keep a real session open beyond three hours on the reference desktop and record the renewal in the test log

features.description: The Google profile applies to Photorealistic 3D Tiles: the Google logo and the copyright of visible tiles are always shown and never covered, and caching, prefetch, offline packaging and non-display use stay off beyond what Google's terms and cache headers allow.
